﻿ Federal Reserve Board - Federal Reserve Board releases results of the 2025 Survey of Consumer Finances, which provides the public and policymakers with detailed insights into the economic condition of American families Skip to main content An official website of the United States Government Here's how you know Official websites use .gov A .gov website belongs to an official government organization in the United States. Main Menu Toggle Button Sections Search Toggle Button Search Search Submit Button Submit Home News & Events Press Releases Press Release October 09, 2026 Federal Reserve Board releases results of the 2025 Survey of Consumer Finances, which provides the public and policymakers with detailed insights into the economic condition of American families For release at 10:00 a.m. EDT Share The Federal Reserve Board on Friday released the results of the 2025 Survey of Consumer Finances, which provides the public and policymakers with detailed insights into the economic condition of American families. The data provide a representative picture of what Americans own, how and how much they borrow, and how they bank. The current version of the survey has been undertaken every three years since 1989 and provides the public with an extensive time series of thorough information on the economic conditions of American families. Alongside the survey data, the Board issued its summary report entitled Changes in U.S. Family Finances from 2022 to 2025 (PDF) , which examines changes in income, net worth, assets, debt, and financial vulnerability. Key findings from the 2025 survey include: Real median family income rose 7 percent between the 2022 to 2025 surveys to $82,200, while real mean family income fell 6 percent to $145,200. Families in the lower ends of the income and net worth distributions saw modest increases in median and mean income, while families in the upper ends saw declines. Between 2022 and 2025, real median net worth rose by 2 percent to $215,900, while real mean net worth rose by 7 percent to $1.24 million. Most families across the net worth and income distributions experienced increases in median and mean wealth. The homeownership rate was 66 percent in 2025, about unchanged from 2022. For families that owned a home, the median net housing value (the value of a home minus home-secured debt, such as a mortgage) rose to $230,000 in 2025 from $218,900 in 2022. Retirement plan participation, which includes account-type plans, individual retirement accounts, or defined benefit plans, was up slightly between 2022 and 2025 at around 65 percent. For families with account-type plans, mean and median balances rose. Participation in the stock market, which includes direct stock and indirect holdings, declined slightly from 58 percent in 2022 to 56 percent in 2025. Conditional on holding stock, median stock holdings grew 36 percent from $56,900 in 2022 to $77,400 in 2025. The fraction of families with any type of debt remained about stable at 77 percent. Median and mean debt outstanding remained unchanged from 2022. The fraction of families with debt payment-to-income ratios greater than 40 percent, which are families with particularly high debt payment obligations relative to their incomes, increased from 6.5 to 8.6 percent, a level last seen in the 2013 survey. In addition to the summary report, an interactive chartbook displaying changes in these financial characteristics over time is available here . Additional data from the survey, including extensive data examining other economic conditions of American families, is made available to researchers and the public here . The survey is conducted for the Board by NORC, a social science research organization at the University of Chicago. Participants in the study are chosen at random from 119 geographic areas, including metropolitan areas and rural counties across the United States, using scientific sampling procedures that aim to produce a sample representative of American families. For media inquiries, please email [email protected] or call (202) 452-2955. Changes in U.S. Family Finances from 2022 to 2025 Evidence from the Survey of Consumer Finances (PDF) Last Update:
            October 09, 2026

title: United States Department of the Treasury Announces New Appointment
body: October 9, 2026 WASHINGTON — Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent announced today a key senior appointment at the U.S. Department of the Treasury. Dr. Judy Shelton will serve as a Counselor in the Office of the Secretary. Shelton is an economist and author specializing in international financial and currency issues. She previously served as U.S. Director of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development and as Chairman of the National Endowment for Democracy. She has testified numerous times before Congress as an expert witness on international financial relations and has consulted with national security officials on global economic developments. At Treasury, Shelton will advise the Secretary on currency policy, with a particular focus on evaluating financial conditions in China. Prior to joining Treasury, Shelton served as a Senior Fellow at the Independent Institute. She also served as a Senior Research Fellow at the Hoover Institution at Stanford University, where she authored The Coming Soviet Crash and Money Meltdown . She holds a Ph.D. in Business Administration from the University of Utah. Shelton began her professional career as a National Fellow at the Hoover Institution, where she received a postdoctoral fellowship to study the impact of Western capital on the Soviet economy. Throughout her career, she has specialized in analyzing the internal monetary and financial conditions of nations and their impact on exchange rates. ###

title: Illegal Alien Convicted at Trial of Child Pornography Charge
body: Press Release Illegal Alien Convicted at Trial of Child Pornography Charge Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Minnesota Garcia Stashed Child Pornography in a Crucifix MINNEAPOLIS – United States Attorney Daniel N. Rosen announced that yesterday a federal jury found Alejandro Rojas Garcia, 65, a Mexican national in the United States illegally, guilty of attempted production of child pornography. The guilty verdict was returned after a four-day trial starting on October 5, 2026, before U.S. District Judge John R. Tunheim. Sentencing will be set at a later date and Garcia faces a mandatory minimum of 180 months in prison. The defendant is also facing state criminal charges for related conduct.¹ Photo of Alejandro Rojas Garcia “Garcia is a predator. A verdict cannot undo the evil he brought on two innocent girls, but it is justice,” said United States Attorney Daniel N. Rosen. According to federal court documents, evidence presented during trial, and as alleged in public state court documents, in early April 2024, law enforcement began an investigation into Garcia after receiving information that he had sexually assaulted two sisters, including Minor Victim 1 and Minor Victim 2, both of whom were then under the age of 13. Garcia was a longtime family friend of the victims’ family, and the family trusted Garcia to care for the children a few days of the week. When Garcia provided childcare for the minor victims, they spent time at Garcia’s apartment. Minor Victim 1 stated that in the spring of 2024, Garcia sexually assaulted her and was violent. Minor Victim 2 stated that, on multiple instances, Garcia would sexually assault her and that he caused her pain. On April 5, 2024, Garcia was arrested. Officers conducted a search of Garcia’s apartment pursuant to a search warrant. The officers seized multiple cellphones, cameras, laptop computers, flash drives, other data storage devices, and a massage gun. Garcia had several hidden cameras placed throughout his apartment, including five cameras hidden in the bathroom. Cameras were aimed at the genital area of a person sitting on the toilet and towards the shower and bath area. Electronic Storage Devices Found in Garcia’s Apartment Officers searched the various storage devices Garcia had stashed in his apartment and found numerous child sexual abuse material, including that of Minor Victim 1 and of other unknown child victims. While searching Garcia’s apartment, an electronic storage detection dog indicated the presence of evidence in a wooden crucifix hanging on a wall in Garcia’s bedroom. Inside the crucifix, behind a bottle of holy water, was a micro-SD card which contained child sexual abuse material involving Minor Victim 1. Front of Crucifix Inside Crucifix Depicting Holy Water and Micro-SD Card At trial, Garcia testified. Under oath, he claimed that he was unaware of the child sexual abuse material on the various devices in his apartment. Regarding the child sexual abuse material involving Minor Victim 1 found on the micro-SD card inside the crucifix, Garcia acknowledged that he put the material on the micro-SD card but denied producing the material with the intent of gratifying his sexual desire. This case was the result of an investigation by Homeland Security Investigations and the Stillwater Police Department, with assistance from Washington County Child Protective Services. Assistant United States Attorneys Dana M. Joseph, Echo D. Fatsis, and William C. Mattessich are prosecuting the case. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorney’s Offices and the Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.justice.gov/psc . ¹ Garcia has been charged by complaint in Washington County District Court File No. 82-CR-24-1329 on two counts of Criminal Sexual Conduct in the 1st Degree. Contact usamn.pressoffice@usdoj.gov Updated October 9, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - Minnesota

title: District of Arizona Charges 345 Individuals for Immigration-Related Criminal Conduct this Week
body: Press Release District of Arizona Charges 345 Individuals for Immigration-Related Criminal Conduct this Week Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Arizona PHOENIX, Ariz. – During the week of enforcement operations from Oct. 3 through Oct. 9, 2026, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Arizona brought immigration-related criminal charges against 345 individuals. Specifically, the United States filed 151 cases in which aliens illegally re-entered the United States, and the United States also charged 172 aliens for illegally entering the United States. In its ongoing effort to deter unlawful immigration, the United States filed 21 cases against 22 individuals responsible for smuggling illegal aliens into and within the District of Arizona. These cases were referred or supported by federal law enforcement partners, including U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s Enforcement and Removal Operations (ICE-ERO), ICE- Homeland Security Investigations (ICE-HSI), U.S. Border Patrol, the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), the FBI, the U.S. Marshals Service (USMS), and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF). Recent matters of interest include: United States of America v. Favela-Favela. On Oct. 5, 2026, Christina Favela-Favela was charged by criminal complaint with Transportation of an Illegal Alien. On Oct. 4, Favela drove a vehicle with her three children to the San Luis, Arizona Port of Entry seeking admission to the United States. Custom and Border Patrol (CBP) officers referred Favela’s vehicle to secondary inspection. CBP officers subsequently learned that on July 7, 2026, Favela had attempted to cross into the United States via the Lukeville, Arizona Port of Entry with two children and a male alien concealed under personal items. With this knowledge, BPAs used a canine unit on Oct. 4 and found a male passenger hiding in the fetal position under personal items in the cargo area of Favela’s vehicle. CPB officers determined the male was an illegal alien without legal authority to be in the United States. [Case Number: 26-MJ-1787] United States v. Luis Angel Diaz-Jimenez. On Oct. 5, 2026, Luis Angel Diaz-Jimenez was charged by criminal complaint with Transportation of an Illegal Alien for Profit. On Oct. 2, Border Patrol Agents (BPAs) attempted to stop a Dodge Charger for an immigration inspection. Instead of yielding to BPAs, the driver, Diaz-Jimenez, accelerated, reaching speeds of approximately 100 mph before leaving the roadway, driving through a fenceline, and coming to a stop in the desert. Three subjects, including the Diaz-Jimenez, then got out of the vehicle and ran. BPAs pursued the subjects on foot and apprehended all three. The two passengers were determined to be citizens of Mexico, unlawfully present in the United States. [Case Number: 26-MJ-10005] A criminal complaint is a formal accusation of criminal conduct. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. RELEASE NUMBER:    2026-171_October 9, 2026 Immigration Enforcement # # # For more information on the U.S. Attorney’s Office, District of Arizona, visit http://www.justice.gov/usao/az/ Follow the U.S. Attorney’s Office, District of Arizona, on Twitter @USAO_AZ for the latest news. Contact Public Affairs Esther Winne Telephone: (602) 514-7740 Esther.Winne@usdoj.gov Updated October 9, 2026 Topic Immigration Component USAO - Arizona Press Release Number: 2026-171_October 9, 2026 Immigration Enforcement

title: Former National Guard task force member sentenced for illegal firearm possession offenses that came to light during an investigation into leaks of sensitive operational information
body: Press Release Former National Guard task force member sentenced for illegal firearm possession offenses that came to light during an investigation into leaks of sensitive operational information Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of California SACRAMENTO, Calif. — Ruby Celly Uribe, 37, of Sacramento, was sentenced today by U.S. District Judge Dena Coggins to two years and five months in prison for unlawfully possession of a machine gun and possession of an unregistered short-barreled rifle, U.S. Attorney Eric Grant announced. On May 26, 2026, a jury found Uribe guilty. According to court documents and evidence presented at a trial, Uribe was assigned to the logistics shop at the California National Guard Headquarters in Mather, and was a member of the Counterdrug Task Force (CDTF). The CDTF supports local, tribal, and federal law enforcement entities in the interdiction of drug trafficking organizations. While assigned to this unit, Uribe leaked information about upcoming drug raids to a person she knew to be involved with drug dealing. Text messages recovered from Uribe’s and the drug dealer’s phones revealed she shared sensitive information about upcoming operations, including the date and location and the number of military vehicles and aircraft involved. A federal search warrant of Uribe’s residence resulted in the discovery of a short-barreled rifle. The firearm had been modified to fire in full-automatic mode as a machine gun. In addition, it was a privately made firearm with no serial number, commonly referred to as a ghost gun. With certain exceptions, federal law prohibits the possession of machine guns and unregistered rifles with barrels shorter than 16 inches. A search of Uribe’s cellphone revealed that she was also engaged in trafficking other nonserialized, short-barreled machine guns, including to a co-worker on July 20, 2022. During preparation for trial in this case, the FBI learned of another illegal firearm that Uribe sold in August 2022. The FBI safely recovered that firearm, which is also a machine gun and short-barreled rifle. The Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives conducted the investigation with assistance from the California Military Department. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Adrian T. Kinsella and Nicole M. Vanek prosecuted the case. Updated October 9, 2026 Topic Firearms Offenses Component USAO - California, Eastern

title: Santa Clarita Man Charged with Federal Arson Offense Alleging He Set Wildfire that Burned Over 1,000 Acres of National Forest Land
body: Press Release Santa Clarita Man Charged with Federal Arson Offense Alleging He Set Wildfire that Burned Over 1,000 Acres of National Forest Land Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Central District of California LOS ANGELES – A Santa Clarita man was charged today in a federal criminal complaint alleging he intentionally set a wildfire in the Angeles National Forest that burned more than 1,000 acres of federally owned land, the Justice Department announced. Rodney Ameile Saba, 70, of Santa Clarita, was charged with arson involving federal property. He is expected to make his initial appearance in U.S. District Court in downtown Los Angeles. According to the complaint, on October 3, 2026, at approximately 2:13 p.m., Saba allegedly ignited what became known as the “Bouquet Fire” behind his residence on Bouquet Canyon Road. Moments before the fire started, Saba allegedly warned a neighbor to expect a loud sound like a shotgun blast. Witnesses then heard a powerful explosion followed by Saba yelling for help and a fire rapidly spreading up the hillside. The complaint alleges that Saba admitted to law enforcement that he threw a cigarette from his porch onto fireworks, causing them to explode and start the fire. Investigators later recovered a lighter, cigarettes, shotgun ammunition, and an aerial mortar firework from Saba’s cabin. Fire investigators with the U.S. Forest Service determined that the Bouquet Fire, which ultimately burned approximately 1,048 acres of federal land, was “probably caused by fireworks” after excluding lightning, campfires, debris burning, and other potential causes. The complaint further alleges that Saba has multiple prior felony convictions, including mayhem, vandalism, possession of a controlled substance, criminal threats, manufacture or possession of a dangerous weapon, and possession of a stolen vehicle. Saba was arrested on October 3, 2026, by local law enforcement on related state charges. Today’s federal complaint formally charges him in federal court. A criminal complaint is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. If convicted, Saba would face a statutory maximum sentence of up to 20 years in federal prison. The United States Forest Service is investigating this matter, with assistance from Los Angeles Sheriff’s Department – Arson Explosives Detail. Assistant United States Attorneys Alexandra Sloan Kelly of the Environmental Crimes and Consumer Protection Section and Brenda N. Galván of the Transnational Organized Crime Section are prosecuting the case. Contact Shawn Lewis Public Information Officer shawn.lewis@usdoj.gov (213) 458-6803 Updated October 9, 2026 Component USAO - California, Central Press Release Number: 26-193

title: Man Sentenced for Role in Smuggling Organization that Kidnapped Migrants and Extorted Their Families; One Dead, Another Missing After Families Paid Ransoms in Vain
body: Press Release Man Sentenced for Role in Smuggling Organization that Kidnapped Migrants and Extorted Their Families; One Dead, Another Missing After Families Paid Ransoms in Vain Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of California Kelly.Thornton@usdoj.gov SAN DIEGO – Isaac Jimenez, a U.S. citizen residing in Tijuana, was sentenced in federal court today to 12 years in prison for his role in a human smuggling conspiracy whose members kidnapped migrants and extorted their families for ransom. Two victims in unrelated kidnappings—a father of four U.S. citizen children and a 21-year-old woman from Tijuana—were never heard from again. The woman was found dead in Tijuana; the man is believed to have been killed in Mexico by Jimenez’s coconspirators. Jimenez crossing the border to pick up ransom money from victim's wife U.S. District Judge Janis L. Sammartino also ordered Jimenez to pay $24,500 in restitution to family members of the victims for funeral and related expenses and for a portion of the ransom payments made during the conspiracy. Judge Sammartino imposed the sentence after the government detailed Jimenez’s extensive history of alien smuggling and his knowing participation in the Tijuana-based organization that used kidnapping, threats and violence against migrants who had paid to be smuggled into the United States. “There’s a fantasy of human smugglers as being on the side of the vulnerable. Then there’s the truth: They are liars, blackmailers and killers. You want proof, keep reading,” said U.S. Attorney Adam Gordon. “Today’s sentencing holds the defendant accountable for knowingly supporting a human smuggling organization that exploited vulnerable people through kidnapping, extortion, threats, and violence,” said Kevin Murphy, Special Agent in Charge of HSI San Diego. “Human smuggling networks profit from human suffering and show a callous disregard for the lives they endanger. HSI will continue working with our law enforcement partners on both sides of the border to identify, investigate, and dismantle those responsible for these crimes.” At today’s hearing, Judge Sammartino described the case events as “the most deliberate and unnecessary loss of life I’ve seen in a very long time.” Addressing Mr. Jimenez, she said, “You preyed upon the most vulnerable people.” Jimenez, who previously lived in Escondido before moving to Tijuana, had been involved in alien smuggling for years before joining the organization in 2024. He was convicted of alien-smuggling offenses in 2015 and 2017 and was arrested again in 2022 in connection with another smuggling investigation. In early 2024, after being released from custody in Mexico, Jimenez began working for members of a Tijuana-based organization, transporting migrants from the border area to locations in the United States for payment. As Jimenez became more involved, he learned that the organization was holding migrants against their will and demanding additional payments from them and their families as a condition of their release. He also received photographs and videos depicting kidnappings and murders involving members of the organization. Despite this knowledge, Jimenez continued to participate in the conspiracy. In September 2024, the organization agreed to smuggle C.G.C., a father of four U.S. citizen children who had previously resided in Southern California, into the United States from Mexico. Instead of being smuggled into the United States, C.G.C. was held captive in Mexico while his kidnappers demanded $30,000 from his family and threatened to kill him. At the direction of his coconspirators, Jimenez collected $15,000 in ransom payments from C.G.C.’s wife, transported the money to Tijuana and delivered it to the kidnappers. Additional ransom demands followed, including demands for money and vehicles. When the family could no longer pay, the kidnappers threatened to provide the location of C.G.C.’s body. Communications eventually ceased. C.G.C. remains missing and, according to court documents, is presumed to have been killed in Mexico by Jimenez’s coconspirators. Three months later, Jimenez agreed to coordinate the smuggling of V.A.E., a 21-year-old Mexican woman, for $7,000. Jimenez was to earn a $1,000 commission. Instead, his coconspirators took V.A.E. to a safe house and held her captive, demanding $30,000 from her family for her release. The kidnappers sent videos showing V.A.E. being threatened with firearms and beaten; they threatened to kill her if the ransom was not paid. V.A.E.’s family eventually paid approximately $10,000, but she was never released. Her skeletal remains were discovered in the Tijuana area in November 2025 and were identified through DNA testing. According to court documents, V.A.E. was likely killed in Mexico by Jimenez’s coconspirators. At today’s hearing, Judge Sammartino described the case events as “the most deliberate and unnecessary loss of life I’ve seen in a very long time.” Addressing Mr. Jimenez, she said, “You preyed upon the most vulnerable people.” Even after the two victims disappeared, Jimenez continued working with the organization and coordinating smuggling operations. Investigators recovered messages from his phone reflecting his continued involvement and awareness of the organization’s use of threats and violence. In one exchange, Jimenez discussed an unidentified woman who was not cooperating and suggested taking her to an office. Other communications among members of the organization referred to making people disappear and torture. Investigators also recovered a video showing a man with his wrists bound as though he had been detained or kidnapped. As part of his guilty plea, Jimenez admitted coordinating alien-smuggling events and collecting ransom payments from family members of migrants who were instead held captive by his coconspirators. The case was investigated by Homeland Security Investigations and the Escondido Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Robert J. Miller and former Special Assistant U.S. Attorneys Alex Biggs and Samson Schatz prosecuted the case. DEFENDANT Case Number 25cr2648-JLS Isaac Jimenez                                                  Age: 30                                    San Diego, CA SUMMARY OF CHARGES Conspiracy to Bring in Certain Aliens – Title 18, U.S.C., Section 371, and Title 8, U.S.C., Section 1324(a)(2)(B)(ii) Maximum penalty: Five years in prison and $250,000 fine Bringing in Aliens for Financial Gain – Title 8, U.S.C., Section 1324(a)(2)(B)(ii) Maximum penalty: Ten years in prison (and a mandatory minimum three years) and $250,000 fine INVESTIGATING AGENCY Homeland Security Investigations This investigation is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF San Diego comprises agents and officers from FBI, Homeland Security Investigations, DEA, ATF, U.S. Marshals, Department of Defense, U.S. Postal Inspection Service, Naval Criminal Investigative Service, IRS Criminal Investigation, U.S. Coast Guard, U.S. Customs and Border Protection and Interpol, with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of California. Contact Kelly Thornton, Director of Media Relations Updated October 9, 2026 Topic Human Smuggling Component USAO - California, Southern Press Release Number: CAS26-1009-Jimenez

title: Canadian Man Sentenced to Prison for Participation in “Grandparent Scam”
body: Press Release Canadian Man Sentenced to Prison for Participation in “Grandparent Scam” Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Vermont USAVT.Press@usdoj.gov BURLINGTON – The United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Vermont stated that on October 6, 2026, Paul Conneh, 39, of Moncton, New Brunswick, Canada, was sentenced by United States District Judge William K. Sessions III to serve a 33-month term of imprisonment for his three weeks of participation in the “grandparent scam.” Judge Sessions also ordered him to pay $256,000 in restitution to the victims of the offense. Previously, on May 28, 2026, Conneh pleaded guilty to conspiring to commit wire fraud and conspiring to launder monetary instruments in connection with the grandparent scam. According to court records, Conneh participated in the grandparent scam by recruiting “bail bondsmen” to travel to the United States, laundering the money they took from elderly Americans, and distributing the money to co-conspirators. Conneh participated in the grandparent scam for three weeks during July and August 2023, victimizing approximately 20 elderly Americans. Conneh was arrested in Costa Rica on January 23, 2025 at the request of the United States, and was extradited to the United States. First Assistant United States Attorney Jonathan A. Ophardt commended the investigative work of Vermont-based agents from Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), United States Customs and Border Protection, and the Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigation, and recognized the assistance provided by HSI in Panama, Interpol, the United States Department of Justice’s Office of International Affairs, the United States Embassy in Costa Rica, and Costa Rica’s Judicial Investigation Department (Organismo de Investigación Judicia) in efforts to secure the arrest and December 2025 extradition. The case was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Nate Burris and Michelle Arra. Conneh was represented by Chandler Matson, Esq. This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Vermont is comprised of agents and officers from Homeland Security Investigations, the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Drug Enforcement Administration, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives, the Diplomatic Security Service, the Internal Revenue Service-Criminal Investigation, and state and local partner agencies, with prosecutions being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Vermont. If you or someone you know has been a victim of elder fraud, help is standing by at the National Elder Fraud Hotline (833-FRAUD-11). This hotline is a free resource created by the U.S. Department of Justice, Office for Victims of Crime for people to report fraud against anyone age 60 or older. Contact Media Inquiries/Public Affairs Officer: (802) 651-8250 Updated October 9, 2026 Topics Elder Justice Homeland Security Task Force Financial Fraud Component USAO - Vermont

title: Jefferson County Man Charged With Threatening FBI Agents When Agents Attempted to Interview Him About Disturbing Calls Made to a Jewish Charity Threatening to “…Put All the Jews in a Gas Chamber and Kill Them”
body: Press Release Jefferson County Man Charged With Threatening FBI Agents When Agents Attempted to Interview Him About Disturbing Calls Made to a Jewish Charity Threatening to “…Put All the Jews in a Gas Chamber and Kill Them” Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of New York USANYN-MediaInquiry@usa.doj.gov Dylan Daniell, age 33, of La Fargeville, NY, was arraigned today October 9, 2026, at the federal courthouse in Syracuse, New York, before United States Magistrate Judge Mitchell J. Katz, after being charged by criminal complaint with threatening a federal law enforcement officer. He was ordered held in custody pending a detention hearing, which is scheduled for October 15, 2026. First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III and Craig L. Tremaroli, Special Agent in Charge of the Albany Field Office of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) made the announcement. The complaint filed against Daniell alleges that in May 2026, a nonprofit Jewish charity organization received several phone calls in which the male caller made inflammatory comments directed at the Jewish community. For example, the caller said, “I would like to blow up Israel and kill all the Jews,” and “I would like to put all the Jews in a gas chamber and kill them.” The FBI identified Daniell as the likely user of the phone number that was used to make the calls to the charity organization. On October 7, 2026, two FBI agents attempted to interview Daniell at his residence in LaFargeville, NY, regarding those phone calls. After the FBI agents introduced themselves and identified themselves as FBI agents, the complaint alleges that Daniell threatened the agents, saying, among other things, “only good cop is a dead cop” and “get the f--- out of here before I pull something out on you.” Approximately 4 hours later, one of the agents received a text message from Daniell’s phone number, which read in part “You ever come to my house again you will not like it. That’s not a threat that’s a promise . . . .” First Assistant U.S. Attorney John A. Sarcone III said, “Let me be absolutely clear: threatening law enforcement officers is not a joke, it is not something that we will brush aside, and it will not be tolerated. Those, like the defendant, as alleged, who believe that they can threaten the men and women who enforce federal law must understand that their actions carry serious consequences. My office will aggressively prosecute these cases and hold offenders accountable to the fullest extent of the law.” “As alleged in the criminal complaint, Mr. Daniell made some disturbing threats to a Jewish charity. When FBI agents went to question him about the allegations, he responded by threatening their lives,” said Craig Tremaroli, Special Agent in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Albany Field Office. “As detailed in the complaint, he followed-up his verbal threats with a text massage saying, ‘…that’s not a threat, that’s a promise.’ Now, he is in custody and the only thing promised for Mr. Daniell is swift justice and potential jail time. The FBI’s response to this incident should send a clear message that we will not tolerate threats of violence toward anyone, especially law enforcement officials who put their lives on the line every day to ensure the safety of our communities. Simply put: if you threaten an FBI agent, be prepared to face some serious consequences.” The charge filed against Daniell carries a maximum sentence of 10 years in prison, a fine of up to $250,000, and a term of supervised release of up to 3 years.  A defendant’s sentence is imposed by a judge based on the particular statute the defendant is convicted of violating, the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other factors. The charges in the complaint are merely accusations. The defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty. FBI is investigating the case, with assistance from New York State Police. Assistant U.S. Attorney Matthew J. McCrobie is prosecuting the case. Updated October 9, 2026 Component USAO - New York, Northern

title: Worcester Man Indicted on Firearm and Drug Distribution Charges
body: Press Release Worcester Man Indicted on Firearm and Drug Distribution Charges Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Massachusetts BOSTON – A Worcester man has been indicted by a federal grand jury for allegedly distributing fentanyl and dealing in firearms without a license. Omar Ramos-Jimenez, 27, was indicted on two counts of distribution of and possession with intent to distribute 40 grams or more of fentanyl, one count of distribution of and possession with intent to distribute fentanyl and one count of dealing in firearms without a license. Ramos-Jimenez was arrested and charged in May 2026 . Ramos-Jimenez was released on conditions following an initial appearance in federal court in Worcester on Sept. 21, 2026. According to the charging documents, between April 8, 2026 and April 16, 2026, Ramos-Jimenez allegedly sold fentanyl and several firearms including a privately manufactured pistol with no serial number, to confidential informants in Worcester. The charge of dealing in firearms without a license provides for a sentence of up to five years in prison, three years of supervised release and a fine of $250,000. The charge of distribution of and possession with intent to distribute 40 grams or more of fentanyl provides for a sentence of no less than five years in prison and up to life, at least four years of supervised release and a fine of up to $5 million. The charge of distribution of and possession with intent to distribute fentanyl provides for a sentence of up to 20 years in prison, at least three years of supervised release and a fine of up to $1 million. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes which govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case. United States Attorney Leah B. Foley; Thomas A. Greco, Special Agent in Charge of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms & Explosives, Boston Field Division; Worcester Police Chief Paul B. Saucier; and Colonel Geoffrey D. Noble, Superintendent of the Massachusetts State Police made the announcement today. Valuable assistance was provided by the Drug Enforcement Administration; Homeland Security Investigations; the Suffolk County Sherrif’s Department; and the Worcester District Attorney’s Office. Assistant U.S. Attorney Brendan O’Shea of the Worcester Branch Office is prosecuting the cases. This case was investigated and prosecuted by the Boston Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) as part of Operation Take Back America . HSTFs, which were established by President Trump in Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion, are joint operations led by the Department of Justice and the Department of Homeland Security. Operation Take Back America is a nationwide federal initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations, and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. Operation Take Back America streamlines efforts and resources from the Department’s Organized Crime Drug Enforcement Task Forces and Project Safe Neighborhood. The details contained in the charging document are allegations. The defendant is presumed to be innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in the court of law. title: Schoharie County Woman Sentenced for $200,000 Fraud
body: Press Release Schoharie County Woman Sentenced for $200,000 Fraud Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of New York USANYN-MediaInquiry@usa.doj.gov Sarah Blood, 44, of Richmondville, New York, was sentenced on September 29, 2026 by United States District Judge Anne M. Nardacci to 5 years’ probation, including 8 months’ home detention, for stealing over $200,000 from the State Agricultural and Rural Leaders, Inc. (SARL) between 2020 and 2023.  First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III and Craig L. Tremaroli, Special Agent in Charge of the Albany Field Office of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), made the announcement. Blood served as the executive director of SARL from August 2019 to October 2023.  SARL is a not-for-profit organization managed by state and local legislators for the purpose of promoting cooperation and education among agricultural and rural communities.  SARL received funding from the United States Food and Drug Administration.  The defendant was responsible for managing SARL’s finances and had access to SARL’s checking account. Between July 2020 and August 2023, Blood stole $203,941.54 from SARL by transferring money from SARL’s bank account to herself or by using SARL’s debit card on unauthorized transactions.  Blood used SARL funds to book a luxury cruise, pay for flights and hotels, and make personal purchases at Amazon and Walmart.  Because of Blood’s theft, SARL had to cancel its 2024 annual conference and engage in emergency fundraising. Blood previously pled guilty to embezzling funds from SARL in April 2026. First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III said: “This case has been under investigation by this Office for three years, and we are glad it has been brought to a successful conclusion.  Sarah Blood was in a position of trust at an organization that received federal funds.  She abused that trust and will now have to repay the money stolen in full.” “Sarah Blood was entrusted to run State Agricultural and Rural Leaders, Inc. (SARL),” said Craig Tremaroli, Special Agent in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Albany Field Office. “Instead, she used that position to blatantly steal over $200,000 – even going so far as to book vacations on the organization’s debit card. The FBI will not turn a blind eye to this kind of fraud. We will continue to work diligently with our law enforcement partners to ensure those committing fraud are held accountable for their actions.” In addition to serving a term of home detention and being placed on probation, Blood is required to make restitution to SARL in the amount of $203,941.54. The FBI investigated the case.  Assistant U.S. Attorneys Matthew Paulbeck and Nicholas Walter prosecuted the case. Updated October 9, 2026 Topic Fraud Component USAO - New York, Northern

title: Oneida County Man Sentenced for Possessing Child Pornography
body: Press Release Oneida County Man Sentenced for Possessing Child Pornography Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of New York USANYN-MediaInquiry@usa.doj.gov James Winston III, age 28, of Utica, New York, was sentenced yesterday to 60 months in federal prison for possession of child pornography announced First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III and Craig L. Tremaroli, Special Agent in Charge of the Albany Field Office of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI). As part of his guilty plea in the case, Winston previously admitted that in March of 2025, several files of child pornography were uploaded to a cloud storage account under his control. Thereafter, on December 10, 2025, Winston was found in possession of two cell phones on which he possessed additional child pornography files including some that depicted the sexual abuse of children as young as three years old. First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III stated: “Any person disturbed enough to seek out and accumulate images and videos depicting the sexual abuse of children deserves years of incarceration. This defendant’s conduct has landed him right where he belongs, in a prison cell.” “Mr. Winston was in possession of multiple devices containing Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM )–some depicting infant victims,” said Craig Tremaroli, Special Agent in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Albany Field Office. “Those depraved actions have just sent him to federal prison for five years. Possessing CSAM perpetuates the abuse of the victims, and the FBI will continue to dedicate every resource needed to investigate and hold these predators accountable for harming our children.” In addition to the term of imprisonment imposed, U.S. District Judge, Anthony J. Brindisi, also imposed a 10-year term of supervision which will begin after Winston is released from prison at which time Winston will also be required to register as a sex offender. This case was investigated by the FBI’s Albany Division Child Exploitation and Human Trafficking Task Force and the New York State Police. Assistant U.S. Attorney Adrian S. LaRochelle prosecuted the case as part of Project Safe Childhood. Project Safe Childhood is a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by the U.S. Attorneys' Offices and the Criminal Division's Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. title: Ex-Postal Worker Admits to Stealing Checks in Massive $34 Million Fraud Scheme
body: Press Release Ex-Postal Worker Admits to Stealing Checks in Massive $34 Million Fraud Scheme Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of Indiana U.S. Attorney’s Office seeking public assistance to reach nearly 6,500 victims INDIANAPOLIS- A former United States Postal Service letter carrier, Destinee Ruffin, 29, of Indianapolis, has pleaded guilty to orchestrating a $34 million conspiracy to commit bank fraud by stealing checks from the U.S. Mail. Ruffin is scheduled to be sentenced on October 27, 2026. This case was brought as part of the Trump Administration’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud. Three of Ruffin’s co-conspirators have already been sentenced for their roles in the scheme. One additional co-conspirator, John Young, is awaiting a sentencing date. The United States Attorney’s Office estimates that approximately 6,500 victims were affected by this widespread fraud scheme. Individuals who believe they may be victims, particularly those who use or live near the Bacon Station Post Office located at 2727 E. 55th Street, Indianapolis, IN 46220 , are encouraged to visit our website for case details and updates. Potential victims may include anyone who lived or worked along the Bacon Station route, mailed a paper check between November 2020 and May 2022, or failed to receive an expected mailing during that period. Due to the large number of victims, it is impractical to notify each one individually. Should you have any questions regarding this case, please contact Victim Witness Coordinator, Stephanie Lloyd at 317-229-2406. Defendant Charge(s) Sentence Restitution Tony McMullen, 36, Calumet Park, IL Conspiracy to commit bank fraud Two years, nine months; three years of supervised release $121,270.30 Eric Hollis, 23, Indianapolis Conspiracy to commit bank fraud One year and one day; three years of supervised release $117,275.30 Kendall Thompson, 24, Indianapolis Conspiracy to commit bank fraud 4 months; three years of supervised release $9,320.05 Destinee Ruffin, 29, Indianapolis Conspiracy to commit bank fraud; theft of mail Sentencing hearing scheduled for October 27, 2026 John Young, 24, Indianapolis Attempt and Conspiracy to commit mail fraud; three counts of Bank fraud Sentencing date pending According to court documents, Ruffin was employed as a letter carrier at the Bacon Station Post Office. Between November 2020 and May 2022, Ruffin used access to both incoming and outgoing mail to steal checks, which he then sold to co-conspirators. In one example, Ruffin and McMullen exchanged 38 Cash App transactions totaling over $10,000 in payments from McMullen to Ruffin for stolen checks. Using the stolen checks, McMullen sought individuals on social media who were willing to deposit altered checks into their bank accounts. These individuals provided debit cards, PINs, or online banking credentials. McMullen altered the payee information on the stolen checks, deposited them, and later withdrew funds or demanded payment through Cash App or Zelle. In total, McMullen fraudulently negotiated 36 checks stolen from Bacon Station, worth approximately $235,632. Ruffin sold even more stolen checks to Young. Young established trusted “mid-level” conspirators, primarily Eric Hollis (Hollis) and Kendall Thompson (Thompson), who deposited stolen checks into various accounts and recruited/ acquired account holders. Young would also list many of the stolen checks for sale on the internet-based application titled “Telegram”. Investigators uncovered the scheme by mailing controlled Treasury checks with recorded serial numbers and tracing them back to Ruffin’s delivery route. In April 2024, officers executed a search warrant on Ruffin’s vehicle, residence, person, and electronic devices. They discovered thousands of stolen checks valued at over $20 million that Ruffin had stolen but not yet sold. In total, Ruffin supplied Young with more than $12 million in stolen checks and provided McMullen with stolen checks worth more than $235,000. The U.S. Postal Service – Office of Inspector General, the United States Postal Inspection Service, and the Treasury Inspector General for Tax Administration investigated this case. The sentences were imposed by U.S. District Court Judge Sarah Evans Barker. U.S. Attorney Wheeler thanked Assistant U.S. Attorney Adam Eakman, who prosecuted this case. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. ### Updated October 9, 2026 Topic Fraud Components National Fraud Enforcement Division USAO - Indiana, Southern

title: Mexican National Arrested for Harboring Illegal Aliens
body: Press Release Mexican National Arrested for Harboring Illegal Aliens Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Arizona PHOENIX, Ariz. – Hector Ambrosio Ruiz, 30, of Mexico, was arrested yesterday and charged by criminal complaint for Harboring Illegal Aliens. On Oct. 7, 2026, agents with Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) executed a federal search warrant at a Phoenix residence suspected of being a stash house for illegal aliens. Upon entering the residence, investigators found twelve individuals hiding in a closet. Ruiz was found among the twelve and was the only one wearing shoes. Law enforcement confirmed that all twelve individuals are citizens of foreign countries without legal authority to reside in the United States. While searching the residence, investigators found multiple pairs of shoes in the backyard and kitchen and a box in the garage containing 12 cellphones. Investigators also observed that the deadbolt locks on the exterior doors of the residence had been replaced with double-cylinder deadbolt locks requiring a key to unlock the doors from both the interior and exterior of the residence. The kitchen and living room of the residence contained no furniture.  Ruiz had his own bedroom and the other 11 illegal aliens slept in one room. Four of the illegal aliens, Hugo Ipolito Ramirez-Vasquez, Eulogio Perez-Sanchez, Santos Antonio Giron-Castro and Obias Alexander Perez-Perez, were also arrested and separately charged with Re-entry of a Removed Alien. Ramirez-Vasquez, Giron-Castro and Perez-Perez were previously removed from the United States in April 2026, and Perez-Sanchez was previously removed in November 2025. A conviction for harboring illegal aliens carries a maximum penalty of 5 years in prison, a fine of $250,000 and a maximum term of three years of supervised release. These cases are part of Operation Take Back America , a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. Operation Take Back America streamlines efforts and resources from the Department’s Organized Crime Drug Enforcement Task Forces (OCDETFs) and Project Safe Neighborhood (PSN). Homeland Security Investigations is conducting the investigation. The U.S. Attorney’s Office, District of Arizona, Phoenix, is handling the prosecution. A criminal complaint is a formal accusation of criminal conduct. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. title: D.C. Fentanyl Dealer Sentenced for Role in Narcotics Trafficking Conspiracy
body: Press Release D.C. Fentanyl Dealer Sentenced for Role in Narcotics Trafficking Conspiracy Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Columbia WASHINGTON – Darae Vaughn, 31, of the District of Columbia, was sentenced today in U.S. District Court to 96 months in federal prison in connection with his role in a narcotics trafficking conspiracy that distributed fentanyl and crack cocaine in Northeast D.C., announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro. “Darae Vaughn trafficked fentanyl and crack cocaine while armed, putting lives at risk,” said U.S. Attorney Pirro. “Now he’s going to prison for eight years. If you push deadly drugs into our community while armed, you will be held accountable. You will go to prison.” Vaughn, aka “Rae,” pleaded guilty June 30, 2026, before Judge Trevor N. McFadden to conspiracy to distribute 40 grams or more of fentanyl, to possession with intent to distribute 28 grams or more of cocaine base, and to distribution and possession of 10 grams or more of fentanyl.  In addition to the 96-month prison term, Judge McFadden ordered Vaughn to serve five years of supervised release. According to court documents, in March 2025 the FBI Safe Streets Task Force began an investigation into reports of narcotics trafficking on the 2000 block of 19th Place SE, particularly counterfeit M30 fentanyl pills. The investigation revealed that from at least April 2025 through September 2025, during nine recorded transactions, Vaughn sold hundreds of fentanyl pills, and quantities of crack cocaine, carfentanyl, and methamphetamine while he was armed with a Glock 43x pistol. In January 2025, codefendant Charles Dixon and Vaughn exchanged text messages discussing pills that Vaughn had supplied to Dixon. Dixon argued with Vaughn about how many pills Vaughn owed him. On April 8, 2025, Dixon participated in the sale of 96 fentanyl pills. On July 3, 2025, Dixon was involved in the sale of 163 fentanyl pills. Dixon was sentenced on October 6 to 33 months in prison for his role in the conspiracy. This investigation was conducted by the FBI Washington Field Office. It was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Iris McCranie and Kate Naseef. This case is part of the Department of Justice’s broader efforts to combat fentanyl trafficking and drug related violence in the District of Columbia. Fentanyl remains one of the deadliest substances circulating in the illegal drug supply, and counterfeit pills containing fentanyl pose extreme risks to unwitting users and the community at large. 25cr306 Updated October 9, 2026 Topic Drug Trafficking Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - District of Columbia

title: D.C. Man Sentenced to 65.5 Years in Prison for Sexually Assaulting Two Victims in 2024
body: Press Release D.C. Man Sentenced to 65.5 Years in Prison for Sexually Assaulting Two Victims in 2024 Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Columbia USADC.Media@usdoj.gov WASHINGTON – Maurice Spears, 34, of Washington, D.C., was sentenced today to a total of 65 years and 180 days in prison for the sexual abuse of two different women in April and July 2024, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro. “Two victims. Eight days of violence, threats, and relentless sexual abuse. Today, the court delivered justice,” said U.S. Attorney Pirro. “Maurice Spears will spend more than 65 years in prison — a consequence that reflects the fear he inflicted and the lives he tried to destroy. This sentence ensures he will never again have the chance to prey on another person in our community.” Spears was found guilty by a Superior Court jury of six counts of first-degree sexual abuse, two counts of felony threats, and one count of misdemeanor sexual abuse on May 14, 2026. Superior Court Judge Jason Park ordered the prison term to be followed by a lifetime supervised release. The defendant must also register as a sex offender. According to the governments evidence, on April 15, 2024, Spears went on a single date with the first victim. After the date, they ended up back in the defendant’s storage unit, where he was living. While inside the storage unit, Spears threatened to kill the victim and her children if she left and told her that he planned to force her into prostitution. He also showed her a fake police badge and told her that he had law enforcement in his pocket. The defendant forced the victim to spend the next three days with him and sexually assaulted the victim twice inside his storage unit. He later took her to Virginia and kept her in a motel room. She was eventually rescued by her family and taken to the hospital. On July 26, 2024, the second victim met Spears when they were both at a services provider for homeless individuals. The defendant promised to help the victim get some shoes. The victim ran into Spears the next day and he started to follow her around and refused to leave her tent when she asked him to. Eventually Spears started threatening her, telling her that he was connected to law enforcement and that he had people who would harm her if he told them to. The defendant spent the next five days repeatedly sexually assaulting her and refused to let her out of his sight. The victim was eventually able to call 911 and escape from the defendant. Spears was arrested on September 9, 2024, and has been in custody since. Joining the announcement was Interim Chief Jeffery Carroll of the Metropolitan Police Department. In announcing the sentence, U.S. Attorney Pirro and Interim Chief Carroll commended the work of those who investigated the case from the Metropolitan Police Department. They also thanked Assistant U.S. Attorneys Sarah Roessler and Amanda Swanson, who prosecuted the case. 2024 CF1 009131 Contact USADC.Media@usdoj.gov Updated October 9, 2026 Topic Violent Crime Component USAO - District of Columbia

title: Former attorney sentenced to two years in prison for stealing from estate he was to probate
body: Press Release Former attorney sentenced to two years in prison for stealing from estate he was to probate Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Washington Took more than $1.5 million for day trading and his living expenses on Bainbridge Island Seattle – A 54-year-old former attorney was sentenced yesterday in U.S. District Court in Seattle to two years in prison for wire fraud for his theft of more than $1.5 million from an estate he was hired to probate, announced Acting U.S. Attorney Charles Neil Floyd. Duncan Connelly voluntarily surrendered his law license as part of his plea agreement on March 5, 2026. At the sentencing hearing U.S. District Judge Jamal N. Whitehead said, “We talk about these financial crimes as if they’re just money,..  but as one of the victim’s wrote, ‘this was the money of someone I loved’… (The victims) had trust in you…. What we’re really talking about is theft. And then you covered it up.” “Mr. Connelly not only stole from his victims, he lied to them about his embezzlement for nearly two years,” said Acting U.S. Attorney Neil Floyd. “His crime was predatory, prolonged, and planned. The victims will likely not be made whole and will have to live the final years of their lives without the financial security that was rightfully theirs.” According to records filed in the case, in July 2020 Connelly was hired by the executor of the estate of a Port Townsend, Washington, woman who left some $3.7 million to six nieces and nephews, with nine specific gifts to various entities. The executor was one of the relatives - all of whom lived overseas - and all were unfamiliar with all of the legal steps necessary to distribute the funds and close the estate. The executor hired Connelly, who then worked at a large prestigious law firm, because of rankings on the firm’s website. Initially, Connelly handled the affairs of the estate appropriately while billing significant legal fees. However, in 2021, Connelly was fired from his large prestigious law firm and went out on his own as a solo practitioner. Connelly began delaying payments and failing to respond to inquiries from the heirs. In February 2023 he began stealing money from the estate. He wrote himself checks from the estate and tried to make it look as if it was a specific bequest. He would deposit the money in his firm account and then transfer it to his personal account to pay his personal expenses. The first check was for $10,000 but the next one in May was for $50,000. Again, he used amounts that made it appear he was paying a specific bequest. All the while he continued to bill fees – some $6,000 for his “work” on the case. Finally in August 2023 Connelly stole $1.5 million from the estate account which he labeled “transfer for investment” to make it look legitimate. But the investment was in risky online day trading and Connelly lost the money. He made some additional partial payments to some of the victims but by July 2024 there was just a little over $500 left in the estate, despite owing the beneficiaries well over $1 million. At this point Connelly stopped responding to the beneficiaries. Connelly ultimately reported his theft to the FBI and federal prosecutors and agreed to give up his law license as part of his guilty plea. In asking for a 30-month sentence prosecutors wrote to the court, “Connelly used his unique position of being the estate’s attorney to commit his crime, knowing his clients had no knowledge of the legal system or estate procedures of this country. Instead of helping the client he was actively billing and ethically required to help, he exploited their inexperience. Connelly had other clients, other opportunities to embezzle client funds, but he chose these victims because they had a large estate and they were uniquely unprepared to challenge Connelly’s lies or detect his fraud from afar.” Judge Whitehead ordered three years of supervised release to follow prison and $1,369,462 in restitution, which accounts for some of the money Connelly paid back after the theft. The case was investigated by the FBI and was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Grace Zoller. Contact Press contact for the U.S. Attorney’s Office is Communications Director Emily Langlie at (206) 553-4110 or Emily.Langlie@usdoj.gov . Updated October 9, 2026 Topics Fraud Financial Fraud Component USAO - Washington, Western

title: Department of Justice Announces Updates to Emergency Scheduling Actions for 7-OH and Related Opioid Substances
body: Press Release Department of Justice Announces Updates to Emergency Scheduling Actions for 7-OH and Related Opioid Substances Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs OAG New actions incorporate updated HHS' science and establish clearer thresholds targeting dangerous, concentrated products The Department of Justice today announced updated emergency scheduling actions targeting 7-hydroxymitragynine (7-OH) and three potent opioid substances related to 7-OH: mitragynine pseudoindoxyl (MGPI), MGM-15, and MGM-16. “Dangerous and addictive opioids do not belong behind convenience store counters,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche. “Our nation’s children and communities deserve protection from harmful substances like 7-OH and other powerful synthetic drugs. The actions taken by the Department of Justice today reflect our commitment to keeping Americans safe and holding drug traffickers accountable.” The U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) is issuing two new Notices of Intent based on new scientific information and recommendations provided by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS). The updated HHS analysis supports a revised threshold approach for 7-OH and MGPI designed to distinguish products containing trace amounts of these substances from formulations that have been intentionally enhanced or concentrated. The two Notices of Intent address: MGM-15 and MGM-16: DEA will reissue the Notice of Intent without changing the current scheduling approach for these substances. 7-OH and MGPI: DEA will issue a new Notice of Intent incorporating HHS' updated scientific recommendation for concentration and ratio thresholds applicable to both substances. HHS recommended that 7-OH and MGPI be subject to Schedule I control when either substance alone, or their combined amount when both are present, exceeds 1 milligram per gram in solid products or 1 milligram per milliliter in liquid products, or when the ratio of mitragynine to 7-OH, MGPI, or their combined amount is less than 100 to 1. HHS recommended this approach to better distinguish products intentionally enhanced or concentrated in these opioid substances from products whose alkaloid composition is more consistent with botanical kratom. The updated HHS analysis confirms that 7-OH occurs naturally in botanical kratom at relatively low levels and identifies additional scientific information suggesting MGPI may also occur at trace levels in some botanical or kratom-derived products. HHS noted that the science concerning the presence of MGPI continues to develop but recommended applying a threshold approach to both 7-OH and MGPI. DEA temporarily placed MGPI, MGM-15, and MGM-16 into Schedule I on August 26, 2026. Those controls will remain in effect during the new 30-day Notice of Intent period and until DEA issues a new temporary scheduling order. For 7-OH, DEA had not yet issued a temporary scheduling order. DEA will reissue a new Notice of Intent reflecting HHS’ updated scientific recommendation. Updated October 9, 2026 Component Office of the Attorney General Press Release Number: 26-1165

title: Rock Island Men Sentenced to Federal Prison for Drug and Gun Charges
body: Press Release Rock Island Men Sentenced to Federal Prison for Drug and Gun Charges Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of Iowa DAVENPORT, Iowa – Rock Island men were sentenced to federal prison for conspiracy to distribute a controlled substance, distribution of a controlled substance, possession with intent to distribute a controlled substance, carrying a firearm during and in relation to a drug trafficking crime, and felon in possession of a firearm. According to public court documents and evidence presented at sentencing, on June 12, 2025, all three men drove together to sell marijuana to a confidential source. Daquez Deasante Howard, 22, remained in the car and possessed money from the drug sale, a loaded, Taurus pistol with an extended magazine, and 20.83 grams of marijuana on his seat. On July 8, 2026, Howard was sentenced to a 68-month prison term, followed by a five-year term of supervised release. Darryl Lee Smith, Jr., 23, was apprehended by police after he ran from the car and possessed a loaded revolver with the hammer cocked back. On May 13, 2026, Smith was sentenced to a 57-month prison term, followed by a three-year term of supervised release Darryl Benard Shears, III,24, ran on foot, escaping the police. Inside the car, police found a loaded pistol, 35.10 grams of cocaine, 14.31grams of crack cocaine, and two functioning scales where Shears had been seated in the car before and after the drug deal. On June 29, 2025, Shears was arrested. Shears again attempted to flee from police on the Arsenal Bridge, crashing into multiple police cars, and jumping into the Mississippi river. Shears also possessed a loaded pistol with a round in the chamber. On October 8, 2026, Shears was sentenced to a 204-month prison term, followed by a six-year term of supervised release. There is no parole in the federal system. United States Attorney David C. Waterman of the Southern District of Iowa made the announcement. The Davenport Police Department investigated the case. Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities. For more information about Project Safe Neighborhoods, please visit Justice.gov/PSN. title: Menands Man Sentenced to Nine Years’ Imprisonment for Child Pornography Offenses
body: Press Release Menands Man Sentenced to Nine Years’ Imprisonment for Child Pornography Offenses Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of New York USANYN-MediaInquiry@usa.doj.gov Jonathan MacDonald, 33, of Menands, New York, was sentenced on October 2, 2026 by United States District Judge Anne M. Nardacci to 9 years’ imprisonment, followed by 15 years’ supervised release, for child pornography offenses.  First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III and Craig L. Tremaroli, Special Agent in Charge of the Albany Field Office of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), made the announcement. MacDonald was charged by indictment in December 2025 with sexually exploiting children, receiving child pornography, and possessing child pornography.  In May 2026, MacDonald pled guilty to the counts of receipt and possession of child pornography.  MacDonald also admitted that in February 2025 he had filmed himself masturbating on a video call with two minor girls who appeared to be from Thailand, and with whom he had connected using the random video-calling app Omegle. MacDonald was arrested after he dropped a flash drive of child pornography in the bathroom at his work and law enforcement identified him as the owner. First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III said: “MacDonald’s abuse of a random video-chatting app was dangerous.  My office will seek to protect child victims everywhere, even on the other side of the world.  MacDonald had previously been investigated for potential child pornography offenses, and we are glad that he has now been successfully prosecuted.” “The fact that Mr. MacDonald brought a flash drive containing child pornography to his workplace illustrates how deeply disturbed his behavior was,” said Craig Tremaroli, Special Agent in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Albany Field Office. “This sentence will keep him locked up for almost a decade without access to any other children he can harm through his depraved online activity. The FBI’s Child Exploitation and Human Trafficking Task Force is steadfast in our mission to aggressively investigate dangerous predators who are seeking to exploit our children and ensure they are sent to prison for their appalling actions.” In addition to serving a term of prison and supervised release, MacDonald is required to pay a total of $27,000 in restitution to the nine identified victims of his offense. The FBI investigated the case.  Assistant U.S. Attorney Nicholas Walter prosecuted the case. Project Safe Childhood is a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by the U.S. Attorneys' Offices and the Criminal Division's Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit https://www.justice.gov/psc . Updated October 9, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - New York, Northern
