title: Four Additional Defendants Plead Guilty in Gun Trafficking Conspiracy
body: Press Release Four Additional Defendants Plead Guilty in Gun Trafficking Conspiracy Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of New Hampshire Av Harris (603) 230-2576 usanh.media@usdoj.gov Case Brought by New Hampshire's Homeland Security Task Force CONCORD – United States Attorney Erin Creegan announced today that four additional defendants have pleaded guilty to federal firearms offenses in connection with an international firearms trafficking conspiracy that funneled illegally obtained weapons from New Hampshire through the Akwesasne Mohawk Indian Reservation in New York. The investigation uncovered that members of the conspiracy trafficked firearms into Canada while also trafficking narcotics and humans into the United States. The four latest defendants to plead guilty in the case between the dates of September 26 and October 9, 2026 are all residents of the Akwesane Mohawk Indian Reservation straddling the U.S.-Canada border from New York to Quebec. They are: Conrad Oakes , 25, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit straw purchasing of firearms and conspiracy to traffic firearms. His sentencing is scheduled for February 23, 2027. Tayson Terrance , 24, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit straw purchasing of firearms and conspiracy to traffic firearms. His sentencing is scheduled for February 19, 2027. Ranonkwatseronhawi Gibson , 22, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit straw purchasing of firearms and conspiracy to traffic firearms. His sentencing is scheduled for February 16, 2027. Montana Cook , 27, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit straw purchasing of firearms and conspiracy to traffic firearms. His sentencing is scheduled for February 16, 2027. Oakes, Terrance, Gibson and Cook were among eight defendants indicted in May 2026. Five other defendants, including Justin Jackson, Melissa Longe, Dustin Tuttle, Caleb Wilcott, and Doug Mulligan, had previously pleaded guilty to firearms offenses arising from the investigation. According to court documents, the investigation began with a firearms trace. A firearm was recovered by the Montreal City Police Department (SVPM) in Montreal, Quebec as part of a search warrant executed in a kidnapping investigation. SVPM recovered a firearm with an obliterated serial number, which they were able to restore. This firearm was purchased by defendant and co-conspirator Dustin Tuttle in New Hampshire. Subsequent investigation revealed a larger conspiracy to smuggle weapons from New Hampshire to Vermont, New York, and ultimately to Canada. ATF and HSI agents learned that the conspiracy utilized the Akwesasne reservation to cross between the U.S. and Canada. One of the defendants utilized jets skis to smuggle contraband, including straw purchased firearms, from the New York portion of the Akwesasne to Cornwall Island. Once the contraband was on Cornwall Island, a resident would then ferry the contraband through the checkpoint and further into Canada. Through this investigation, the ATF and HSI learned that drugs, humans, and guns were trafficked to and from Canada utilizing Cornwall Island. ATF and HSI have identified approximately 51 firearms potentially trafficked from New Hampshire to Canada through Vermont and the Akwesasne reservation in New York and Canada, at least ten of which were subsequently recovered at various Canadian crime scenes, in Canada. For example, after an attempted shooting in a parking lot in Montreal, Canadian law enforcement was able to find the discarded firearm which was used. That firearm was purchased by defendant and member of the conspiracy, Melissa Longe, from a Federal Firearms Licensee in Winchester, New Hampshire. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives This investigation was led by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) and Homeland Security Investigations (HSI). The Ontario Provincial Police (OPP), Sûreté du Québec (SQ), Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA), U.S. Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS), Customs and Border Protection (CBP), Saint Regis Mohawk Tribal Police (SRMTP), Akwesasne Mohawk Police Service (AMPS), New York Department of Corrections and Community Supervision-Office of Special Investigations, Manchester Police Department, and the Keene Police Department have provided valuable assistance. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives “These defendants have admitted to operating a sophisticated firearms trafficking network that exploited New Hampshire gun dealers, straw purchasers, and the international border to move dozens of firearms into Canada, facilitating further trafficking crime and violent crimes,” said Erin Creegan, United States Attorney for the District of New Hampshire. “Guns purchased in New Hampshire and traded through this criminal enterprise were later recovered at crime scenes involving offenses such as kidnapping and attempted murder. We are grateful for the partnership between our federal agencies, Canadian and tribal authorities, as well as state and local law enforcement in New Hampshire and New York that helped investigate these crimes and take down this dangerous network.” Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives “These convictions demonstrate the effectiveness of intelligence-driven policing and cooperative law enforcement efforts in bringing criminal charges against firearm traffickers. Crime gun intelligence connected firearms recovered at different crime scenes in Canada, advancing our Canadian partner’s domestic investigations into violent crime while simultaneously alerting ATF to a transnational firearms trafficking scheme at work in the United States. The guilty pleas hold accountable individuals who exploited that access to firearms and the freedom to travel while undermining public safety in both countries. ATF is proud of our partnerships with our federal, state, local and international law enforcement partners and will continue to work together to build safe communities on both sides of the border,” said Thomas Greco, Special Agent in Charge of ATF Boston Field Division. “These guilty pleas demonstrate the serious consequences of trafficking firearms across international borders and into communities where they can fuel violent crime. This case is a powerful example of what can be accomplished when law enforcement partners share intelligence, resources, and expertise across jurisdictions and borders. ATF remains committed to identifying, disrupting, and dismantling firearms trafficking networks that threaten public safety. We commend the outstanding work of ATF Boston and ATF New York Albany personnel, HSI New York, Saint Regis Mohawk Tribal Police, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of New Hampshire, and our Canadian law enforcement partners whose persistence and collaboration brought these defendants to justice,” said Bryan DiGirolamo, Special Agent in Charge of ATF’s New York Field Division. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives The charge of conspiracy to straw-purchase firearms provides a maximum prison term of 25 years, a maximum fine of $250,000, and not more than five years of supervised release. The charge of conspiracy to traffic firearms provides a maximum prison term of 15 years, a maximum fine of $250,000, and not more than three years of supervised release. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes which govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case. This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF New Hampshire comprises agents and officers from FBI, HSI, IRS, DEA, ATF, USMS, and DSS with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the District of New Hampshire. Special Assistant U.S. Attorney Christopher Marin, Assistant U.S. Attorney Yasir Sadat, and Paralegal Specialist Kristina McNamara are handling the prosecution on behalf of the United States. title: Shelbyville Man Pleads Guilty to Receipt of Child Sexual Abuse Material and Other Charges
body: Press Release Shelbyville Man Pleads Guilty to Receipt of Child Sexual Abuse Material and Other Charges Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Kentucky Frankfort, Ky. – A Shelbyville man, Natividad Aguilera Garcia, 40, pleaded guilty on Friday, October 9, 2026, before Chief U.S. District Judge David L. Bunning to receipt of child sexual abuse material, inducing illegal immigration, making false statements to the United States, and presenting false documentation to the United States. According to his plea agreement, Garcia, a Honduran citizen and legal permanent resident of the United States, met a minor while visiting family in Honduras. The minor reported that, while in Honduras, Garcia courted her. Upon his return to the United States, Garcia received sexually explicit images of the minor. The minor reported, and electronic evidence shows, that Garcia persuaded the minor to illegally enter the United States. Once in the United States, the minor went to a shelter for unaccompanied alien children, overseen by the Office of Refugee Resettlement (“ORR”), a sub-agency of Health and Human Services. Thereafter, Garcia falsely represented to ORR that he was the minor’s uncle, also presenting a false Honduran birth certificate to establish the familial relationship. ORR relied on these falsehoods and decided to place the minor in Garcia’s care. Garcia picked the minor up from the Louisville airport. Days after picking up the minor, Garcia’s ex-wife reported Garcia’s conduct to the shelter, prompting law enforcement’s investigation. Garcia’s plea agreement does not contain admissions regarding his conduct with the minor after he picked her up from the airport. However, soon after law enforcement contacted Garcia about the minor’s whereabouts, Garcia searched the internet for information about how long after intercourse sexual contact can be detected. Garcia was indicted in March 2024. The court docket indicated several delays associated with Garcia obtaining new counsel. “This prosecution demonstrates federal law enforcement’s commitment to protecting children outside of our borders from conduct that originates within our borders; ensuring the integrity of our borders; and deterring those who would lie to the United States government to gain custody of an alien child for nefarious purposes,” said Jason Parman, U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of Kentucky. “HSI is committed to protecting vulnerable individuals - including unaccompanied alien children - and holding accountable those who use deception, fraud, and exploitation to victimize others,” said HSI Nashville acting Deputy Special Agent in Charge Michael Perez. “Working alongside our federal, state, and local partners, we will continue to investigate these complex cases, support victims, and pursue those who violate the law.” “Today’s guilty plea underscores the critical importance of protecting vulnerable children from those who seek to exploit them,” said Jason E. Meadows, Special Agent in Charge of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General (HHS-OIG). “This case demonstrates the strength of our partnerships with Homeland Security Investigations, the Kentucky State Police, and the Shelbyville Police Department.  Together, we remain steadfast in our commitment to pursuing those who prey upon minors, holding those who commit such crimes accountable, and safeguarding the integrity of federal programs designed to protect children.” Jason Parman, United States Attorney for the Eastern District of Kentucky; Dennis M. Fetting, Special Agent in Charge, Homeland Security Investigations-Nashville; Jason E. Meadows, Special Agent in Charge, U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of the Inspector General; Phillip J. Burnett, Jr., Commissioner of the Kentucky State Police; and Bruce W. Gentry, Shelbyville Police Department; jointly announced the guilty plea. The investigation was conducted by Homeland Security Investigations, Health and Human Services’ Office of Inspector General, Shelbyville Police Department, and Kentucky State Police.  The U.S. Attorney’s Office was represented by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Mary Melton and Aubrey Girouard. Garcia is scheduled to be sentenced on February 10, 2027. He faces a minimum of five years and a maximum of twenty years in prison, in addition to a $250,000 fine (if applicable). However, any sentence will be imposed by the Court, after its consideration of the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and the federal sentencing statutes. This case was prosecuted as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the Criminal Division’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.projectsafechildhood.gov . — END — Contact CONTACT:  Jenny Parker PHONE:  (859) 685-4906 E-MAIL: jenny.parker@usdoj.gov Updated October 9, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - Kentucky, Eastern

title: Gainesville Man Pleads Guilty to Convenience Store Robbery
body: Press Release Gainesville Man Pleads Guilty to Convenience Store Robbery Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Florida Gainesville, Florida – Denzel Dyshaun Flagg, 27, of Gainesville, Florida, pleaded guilty in federal court to one count of Hobbs Act Robbery. The plea was announced by John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida. U.S. Attorney Heekin said: “This successful prosecution was made possible by the excellent investigative work of our state and federal law enforcement partners, who tracked down this defendant so we could hold him accountable for his role in this violent crime. We owe it to our citizens to protect them from the predations of violent criminals and to seek maximum punishment to hold those offenders accountable and deter future crime.” Court documents reflect that on February 18, 2025, the defendant participated in the robbery of the Eastside Food Store in Gainesville, Florida. During the robbery, two other individuals entered the store wearing ski masks, and one of them pointed a gun directly at the face of the store clerk before stealing cash from the register. The defendant acted as the getaway driver. Flagg faces a maximum sentence of twenty years’ imprisonment. Sentencing is scheduled for November 3, 2026, at the United States Courthouse in Gainesville before United States Chief District Judge Allen C. Winsor. The case involved a joint investigation by the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Alachua County Sherriff’s Office. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorneys Adam Hapner and James McCain. Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities . title: Two Women Charged with Helping Violent Inmates Escape from DeKalb County Jail
body: Press Release Two Women Charged with Helping Violent Inmates Escape from DeKalb County Jail Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Georgia ATLANTA — A federal grand jury indicted Melayna Whatley and Gabriela Ortis for allegedly helping three inmates, including a federal prisoner serving a life sentence, escape from the DeKalb County Jail in December 2025. “Every jailbreak puts the public at risk,” said U.S. Attorney Theodore S. Hertzberg. “Thankfully, quick action by numerous law enforcement agencies ensured the lightning-fast capture of the men who escaped from DeKalb County late last year. Now, the women who allegedly helped them bust free must face the consequences for unleashing terror into our community.” “This was far more than an escape from jail—it put an innocent member of the public directly in harm’s way,” said Marlo Graham, Special Agent in Charge of FBI Atlanta. “These defendants allegedly helped violent fugitives evade capture, and their actions contributed to a dangerous chain of events that ended with an innocent woman being kidnapped and held against her will. The FBI and our law enforcement partners will continue to hold accountable anyone who assists violent offenders and puts our communities at risk.” According to U.S. Attorney Hertzberg, the indictment, and other information presented in court: In June 2025, Stevenson Charles was sentenced in the Southern District of Florida to life in prison for carjacking, kidnapping, bank robbery, and brandishing a firearm. On December 5, 2025, the U.S. Marshals Service transferred him to the DeKalb County Jail in Decatur, Georgia, to face additional state charges. On December 21, 2025, Charles and fellow inmates Yusuf Minor and Noad Yohannes, acting in concert, escaped from the DeKalb County Jail and fled to Florida with the alleged assistance of Melayna Whatley and Gabriela Ortis. Whatley allegedly served as the outside conduit for the escape by making phone calls and text messages on Minor’s behalf to locate a getaway driver before the escape. On the night of the escape, Whatley allegedly allowed Charles, Minor, and Yohannes to use her Flat Shoals Road residence to temporarily evade capture and to use her cellular telephone to contact additional co-conspirators. Gabriela Ortis allegedly arranged the escapees’ transportation on the night of the escape by hiring them a Lyft rideshare driver. After the escapees entered the Lyft vehicle, Charles, Minor, and Yohannes allegedly put an item around the driver’s neck, dragged her into the backseat, tied her hands together, threatened her, and drove her vehicle nearly 700 miles to Broward County, Florida with her inside. Law enforcement captured the escapees and rescued the Lyft driver on December 22, 2025. On February 27, 2026, a federal jury in Fort Lauderdale found Charles guilty of conspiracy to commit kidnapping, kidnapping, Hobbs Act robbery, and possession of a firearm and ammunition by a convicted felon. On March 27, 2026, Minor pled guilty to conspiracy to commit kidnapping, kidnapping, and Hobbs Act robbery. On May 5, 2026, a federal jury in Fort Lauderdale found Yohannes guilty of the same three crimes. On September 23, 2026, a federal grand jury in Atlanta indicted Melayna Whatley, 30, of DeKalb County, Georgia, and Gabriela Ortis, 22, of Miami, Florida, on charges of conspiracy to aid and assist escape, aiding and assisting an escape, and harboring and concealing an escaped prisoner. Law enforcement arrested Whatley on September 29, 2026, and Ortis appeared in federal court yesterday following her arrest. Members of the public are reminded that the indictment only contains charges. The defendants are presumed innocent of the charges, and it will be the government’s burden to prove the defendants’ guilt beyond a reasonable doubt at trial. This case is being investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation, with valuable assistance provided by the United States Marshals Service and DeKalb County Sheriff’s Office. For further information please contact the U.S. Attorney’s Public Affairs Office at USAGAN.PressEmails@usdoj.gov or (404) 581-6185. The Internet address for the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Georgia is http://www.justice.gov/usao-ndga . Updated October 9, 2026 Topic Violent Crime Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Georgia, Northern

title: Syracuse Man Charged With Receiving Child Pornography
body: Press Release Syracuse Man Charged With Receiving Child Pornography Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of New York USANYN-MediaInquiry@usa.doj.gov Thomas Pennington, age 57, of Syracuse, New York, appeared in federal court October 2, 2026, on charges of receiving child pornography. Pennington was detained pending further proceedings. First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III and Anthony Patrone, Acting Special Agent in Charge of the Buffalo Field Office of Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) made the announcement. The complaint filed against Pennington alleges that on or about October 1, 2026, Pennington received child pornography on multiple electronic devices.  Pennington admitted to using the internet to find and download child pornography files. First Assistant U.S. Attorney John A. Sarcone said, “When Pennington searched the internet, as alleged, for child pornography and received those files on his devices, he may have thought his victimization of the children depicted would go undetected.  But thanks to our partners at HSI, Pennington will face the court and be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law for his heinous actions.” “Thomas Pennington's alleged conduct represents deeply disturbing exploitation that perpetuates the abuse of children and compounds the lasting trauma endured by victims," said HSI Buffalo Acting Special Agent in Charge Anthony Patrone. "One exploited child is one too many, and every instance demands a determined response. HSI Syracuse remains steadfast in working alongside our law enforcement partners to hold offenders accountable, combat child exploitation, and protect the most vulnerable members of our communities.” The receipt charge filed against Pennington carries a mandatory minimum term of 5 years in prison and a statutory maximum prison term of 20 years. The charge also carries a fine of up to $250,000 and a term of supervised release of at least 5 years and up to life. Pennington will also be required to register as a sex offender upon his release from prison. A defendant’s sentence is imposed by a judge based on the particular statutes the defendant is convicted of violating, the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other factors. The charges presented are merely accusations. The defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty. This case was investigated by HSI.  Assistant U.S. Attorney A.J. Vickey is prosecuting the case as part of Project Safe Childhood. Project Safe Childhood is a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by the U.S. Attorneys' Offices and the Criminal Division's Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit https://www.justice.gov/psc . Updated October 9, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - New York, Northern

title: Total of Four Defendants Plead Guilty in Connection with Widespread  Child Exploitation Conspiracy
body: Press Release Total of Four Defendants Plead Guilty in Connection with Widespread  Child Exploitation Conspiracy Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of New York USANYN-MediaInquiry@usa.doj.gov Four defendants have now pled guilty in connection with a multi-jurisdictional child exploitation conspiracy that included the trafficking of child pornography produced during the conspiracy. First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III, Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) Buffalo Acting Special Agent in Charge Anthony Patrone, and New York State Police (NYSP) Superintendent Steven G. James made the announcement. The defendants involved in the case are: Devin LaValley, age 38, of Burlington, New York; Melissa McDougal, age 30, of Pulaski, New York; Grace Balthazor, age 34, of Elmira, New York; and Roxanne Clark, age 45, of Bristol, Vermont. As part of their guilty pleas, the defendants admitted to their respective involvement in a years-long child exploitation conspiracy and the trafficking of child pornography produced during the conspiracy. LaValley admitted that, years ago, he began intimate relationships with both Balthazor and McDougal, both of whom had access to children. LaValley admitted to then conspiring with both women to get close to the children in their care for the purpose of sexually abusing the children and creating photos and videos depicting that abuse. McDougal and Balthazor also admitted to conspiring with LaValley to abuse the children for the purpose of creating child pornography. LaValley also admitted that after he created the child pornography with McDougal and Balthazor’s assistance, he then distributed the child sexual abuse material to Clark, another woman with whom LaValley had an intimate relationship. For her part, Clark admitted to receiving the child pornography LaValley, McDougal, and Balthazor had produced as part of online communications with LaValley in which she and LaValley discussed their mutual interest in sexually abusing children. At sentencing, LaValley, McDougal, and Balthazor face a mandatory minimum term of 15 years in federal prison and maximum sentence of 30 years for the conspiracy charge. The receipt and distribution charges to which Clark and LaValley have pled guilty carry a mandatory minimum term of five years in federal prison and maximum terms of 20 years. Each charge carries a fine of up to $250,000, and a term of supervised release of at least 5 years and up to life. A defendant’s sentence is imposed by a judge based on the particular statutes the defendant is convicted of violating, the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other factors. First Assistant U.S. Attorney Sarcone stated, “I commend HSI and the New York State Police for the incredible investigative work that led to these four convictions. I also want to acknowledge the urgency with which HSI and State Police identified and arrested the various defendants, several of whom lived in other districts. The result of their diligent work was the identification and protection of multiple children who likely would have continued to be victimized by the defendants had it not been for the dedicated agents and investigators involved. My office remains steadfast in its commitment to work closely with our federal, state, and local partners to do whatever we can to protect our communities from the threat posed by individuals, like the defendants here, who seek to harm the most vulnerable among us.” Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) Buffalo Acting Special Agent in Charge Anthony Patrone said, “Those who exploit children and trade in images of their abuse inflict profound and lasting harm on victims, families, and entire communities. These guilty pleas hold all four defendants accountable for their roles in a calculated, years-long conspiracy that preyed on vulnerable children and perpetuated their victimization through the production and distribution of child sexual abuse material. HSI Syracuse and our law enforcement partners will pursue every available lead to identify predators, disrupt child-exploitation networks and safeguard children in our communities.” NYSP Superintendent James stated, “Child predators will go through extreme lengths to exploit children and conduct the most reprehensible of acts. As we fight for the victims and all those affected, we hope the justice brought forth provides a sense of peace that these individuals will never commit a crime like this again. I thank our State Police members, the United States Attorney’s Office, and the Buffalo Field Office of Homeland Security Investigations for their consistent, proactive work on this case.” HSI and NYSP investigated the case with the assistance of the Office of the Vermont Attorney General. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Adrian S. LaRochelle as a part of Project Safe Childhood. Project Safe Childhood is a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by the U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the Criminal Division’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit https://www.justice.gov/psc . Updated October 9, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - New York, Northern

title: Azerbaijani National Pleads Guilty to $1 Million Wire Fraud and Money Laundering Scheme Against the United States Postal Service
body: Press Release Azerbaijani National Pleads Guilty to $1 Million Wire Fraud and Money Laundering Scheme Against the United States Postal Service Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Middle District of Florida Orlando, Florida – Khayyam Arif Oglu Farajov (40), an Azerbaijani national, has pleaded guilty to one count of wire fraud and one count of money laundering in connection with a scheme to fraudulently obtain payments from the United States Postal Service (USPS). Farajov faces a maximum penalty of 20 years in federal prison on each count. A sentencing date has not yet been set. U.S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement. According to the plea agreement, Farajov owned and operated Talishco LLC, a trucking and freight brokerage company in Orlando. In May 2022, Farajov enrolled Talishco in the USPS “Freight Auction” program to transport bulk mail for the USPS. Between June 2022 and January 2023, Farajov bid on and was awarded hundreds of contracts to transport mail across the country on behalf of the USPS. After being awarded the contracts, Farajov routinely and intentionally did not send trucks to do the work. When USPS staff asked where the trucks were, he made false excuses, such as claiming he had lost contact with his drivers or that they were running behind schedule, which forced the USPS to reassign the work to other carriers. Farajov then went back into the platform and exploited the system by falsely marking the loads as delivered and triggering payment from USPS even though he had not performed the contracted routes. Farajov obtained more than $1 million from this scheme. After he received the funds, he funneled them through a series of bank accounts belonging to shell companies he owned. After reconsolidating the fraud proceeds into two personal investment brokerage accounts, Farajov invested the fraud proceeds in the stock market for his personal enrichment. The United States traced the fraud proceeds and seized the contents of Farajov’s brokerage accounts. Farajov has agreed to forfeit the seized brokerage accounts and pay an additional $993,979 in restitution to the USPS. This case was investigated by the United States Postal Service – Office of Inspector General. It is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Richard Varadan. The forfeiture is being handled by Assistant United States Attorney Nicole Andrejko. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division. The core mission of the Fraud Division is to zealously investigate and prosecute those who steal or fraudulently misuse taxpayer dollars.  Department of Justice efforts to combat fraud support President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. Updated October 9, 2026 Topic Financial Fraud Component USAO - Florida, Middle

title: First-Time Offender Sentenced to 27 Years in Federal Prison for Attempted Coercion of a Minor
body: Press Release First-Time Offender Sentenced to 27 Years in Federal Prison for Attempted Coercion of a Minor Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Middle District of Florida Tampa, Florida – Jonathan Edward Veselka (45, Arizona) was sentenced by U.S. District Judge John L. Badalamenti to 27 years in federal prison, followed by a lifetime term of supervised release, for attempted coercion and enticement of a minor to engage in sexual activity, attempted transportation of a minor with intent to engage in sexual activity, and attempted transfer of obscene material to a minor. Veselka pleaded guilty on June 22, 2026. United States Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement. According to court documents, for approximately three weeks, Veselka communicated with an undercover officer, believing it was a 14-year-old girl. Veselka sent the undercover officer sexual photos and videos of himself, asked the undercover explicit sexual questions, and detailed the sexual activity he wished to engage in with the individual he believed to be a 14-year-old girl. Veselka arranged for the purported 14-year-old girl to travel to Las Vegas to engage in sexual activity with him. Veselka had never been arrested prior to this criminal offense. This case was investigated by Homeland Security Investigations. It was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorneys Abigail K. King and Courtney Derry. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by United States Attorneys’ Offices and the Criminal Division’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who sexually exploit children, and to identify and rescue victims. title: Davenport Man Sentenced to Five Years in Federal Prison for Firearm Charges
body: Press Release Davenport Man Sentenced to Five Years in Federal Prison for Firearm Charges Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of Iowa DAVENPORT, Iowa – A Davenport man was sentenced on October 8, 2026, to five years in federal prison for possessing a firearm as a felon. According to public court documents and evidence presented at sentencing, Terry Lee Chance, Jr., 33, drove through Davenport in possession of a .40 caliber pistol with an obliterated serial number. Officers with the Davenport Police Department recovered the pistol during a traffic stop of the vehicle Chance drove. After completing his term of imprisonment, Chance will be required to serve a three-year term of supervised release. There is no parole in the federal system. United States Attorney David C. Waterman of the Southern District of Iowa made the announcement. The Davenport Police Department investigated the case. Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities. For more information about Project Safe Neighborhoods, please visit Justice.gov/PSN. title: Homeland Security Task Force Investigation Leads To Conviction of Albany Man For Crack Cocaine Sales
body: Press Release Homeland Security Task Force Investigation Leads To Conviction of Albany Man For Crack Cocaine Sales Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of New York USANYN-MediaInquiry@usa.doj.gov Kymere Thomas, 28, of Albany, New York, pled guilty before U.S. District Judge Anthony Brindisi on October 5, 2026, to distributing crack cocaine.  First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III and Craig L. Tremaroli, Special Agent in Charge of the Albany Field Office of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), made the announcement. Between March and August 2025, Thomas sold over 50 grams of cocaine, and over 580 grams of crack (cocaine base), in eight separate transactions.  In one of these transactions alone Thomas sold 292 grams of crack, for which he was paid over $11,000.  When officers searched his residence, they found another 650 grams of cocaine and 15 grams of crack.  Thomas was arrested in September 2025 and remained on pre-trial release until his guilty plea, when he was remanded to custody. First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III stated, “We will aggressively work to dismantle the drug-trafficking networks that threaten the safety of our communities. Our work is far from over, and this guilty plea shows those who choose to spread dangerous narcotics that we are coming for you.  I am grateful to our law enforcement partners for arresting him and that he is finally off our streets.” “By his own admission, Mr. Thomas was responsible for trafficking an enormous amount of cocaine into our communities,” said Craig Tremaroli, Special Agent in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Albany Field Office. “FBI Albany’s Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) responded with the full weight of its federal, state, and local partnerships, and now Mr. Thomas is heading to federal prison for a least a decade. The FBI is laser-focused on investigating and holding accountable any criminal looking to endanger our communities through the sale of illegal drugs.” Thomas faces a mandatory minimum term of imprisonment of 10 years, followed by a minimum term of 5 years’ supervised release.  A defendant’s sentence is imposed by a judge based on the particular statutes the defendant is convicted of violating, the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other factors.  Thomas’s sentencing has been scheduled for January 27, 2027. The FBI investigated the case.  Assistant U.S. Attorney Nicholas Walter prosecuted the case. This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Buffalo comprises agents and officers from Homeland Security Investigations, the FBI, ATF, IRS Criminal Investigations, Department of Homeland Security Emergency Removal Operations, Customs and Border Protection, the DEA, the U.S. Coast Guard Investigative Service, the U.S. Marshals Service, U.S. Postal Inspection Service, the U.S. Secret Service, and the Diplomatic Security Service, with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of New York. body: Press Release Louisville Man Charged with Escape from Federal Custody and Possession of a Firearm by a Prohibited Person Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Kentucky Louisville, KY – A federal grand jury in Louisville, Kentucky, returned an indictment on October 7, 2026, charging a Louisville man with escape from federal custody and possession of a firearm by a prohibited person. According to the indictment, Damion Lamont Hayes, 26, of Louisville, Kentucky, was charged with escaping from federal custody on or about April 22, 2026, in Jefferson County, Kentucky. At the time of the alleged escape, Hayes was serving a 91-month federal prison sentence imposed following a judgment and conviction in the Western District of Kentucky, Case No. 3:20-CR-00054, for aiding and abetting carjacking. Hayes was confined at the Dismas Charity Center Residential Reentry Center under the authority of the Federal Bureau of Prisons when he allegedly escaped from custody. Additionally, Hayes was charged with possession of a firearm by a prohibited person. Hayes was prohibited from possessing a firearm because he had previously been convicted of the following felony offenses. On February 4, 2021, in United States District Court for the Western District of Kentucky, Case No. 3:20-CR-00054, Hayes was convicted of the offense of carjacking – aiding and abetting. On February 5, 2021, in Jefferson Circuit Court, Case No. 18-CR-3427-02, Hayes was convicted of the offenses of facilitation to murder and facilitation to robbery in the first degree. On February 5, 2021, in Jefferson Circuit Court, Case No. 20-CR-1273, Hayes was convicted of the offense of possession of a handgun by a convicted felon. If convicted as charged in the indictment, Hayes faces a combined mandatory maximum sentence of 20 years in prison. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the sentencing guidelines and other statutory factors. There is no parole in the federal system. This case is being investigated by the United States Marshals Service and Louisville Metro Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Kayla M. Campbell is prosecuting the case. title: Final Two Defendants Sentenced in Fentanyl Distribution Resulting in Overdose Death
body: Press Release Final Two Defendants Sentenced in Fentanyl Distribution Resulting in Overdose Death Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Kentucky COVINGTON, Ky. – Two men, Ryan Cooley, of Cincinnati, Ohio, and Nicholas Sturgill, of Villa Hills, Ky., were sentenced on Thursday to prison terms of 12.5 years and 10 years, respectively, by Chief U.S. District Judge David Bunning for distribution of fentanyl resulting in death. An investigation revealed that on May 21, 2025, Nathaniel Ferguson, Cooley and Sturgill’s co-defendant, sold approximately 50 pressed pills containing fentanyl and xylazine to Cooley. Cooley then sold the pills to Sturgill, who brought them to his Kenton County residence and shared them with the victim, who died the next day. Toxicology results and autopsy findings confirmed that the victim’s death resulted from an overdose involving fentanyl and xylazine. During the investigation, agents recovered additional blue pills and drug paraphernalia from the residence, all of which tested positive for fentanyl and xylazine. Sturgill admitted to purchasing such pressed pills from Cooley for approximately one year, including those involved in the fatal incident, and provided text messages corroborating the transactions. Surveillance footage from the May 21 sale further confirmed Cooley’s involvement and showed him arriving at the scene of the drug transaction in a vehicle driven by Ferguson. Under law enforcement direction, Sturgill conducted controlled purchases of pills from Cooley on multiple dates in June and July 2025. Laboratory testing revealed that the pills contained various dangerous substances, including fentanyl analogues, xylazine, ketamine, and carfentanil. Agents later executed a search warrant at Cooley’s residence, where he admitted to supplying the pills and identified Ferguson as his source. Cooley’s communications with Ferguson confirmed their relationship. A subsequent controlled purchase arranged through Cooley led to the recovery of additional pills supplied by Ferguson, which again tested positive for fentanyl-related substances. Ferguson was sentenced on September 16, 2026, to 22 years in prison for his role in fentanyl distribution leading to the victim’s death by overdose. “This case is another tragic example of the devastation caused by illicit fentanyl, and it is the third fentanyl distribution case resulting in an overdose death to be sentenced in our district in the past month,” said U.S. Attorney Jason Parman. “We will continue working with our law enforcement partners to identify those who distribute these dangerous drugs and hold them accountable when their actions result in the loss of life.” Jason Parman, United States Attorney for the Eastern District of Kentucky; Jim Scott, Special Agent in Charge, DEA, Louisville Field Division; Scott Hardcorn, Director of the Northern Kentucky Drug Strike Force, and Chief Matthew Hall, Villa Hills Police Department, jointly announced the sentence. The investigation was conducted by the DEA, the Northern Kentucky Drug Strike Force, and the Villa Hills Police. Assistant U.S. Attorney Tony Bracke is prosecuting the case on behalf of the United States. – END – Contact CONTACT:  Jenny Parker PHONE:  (859) 685-4906 E-MAIL: jenny.parker@usdoj.gov Updated October 9, 2026 Topics Drug Trafficking Opioids Component USAO - Kentucky, Eastern

title: Wales murder investigation remains active some 25 years after fatal shooting
body: Press Release Wales murder investigation remains active some 25 years after fatal shooting Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Washington Law enforcement urges anyone with information to come forward Seattle – Just days before the 25 th anniversary of the unsolved murder of Assistant U.S. Attorney Thomas C. Wales, law enforcement leaders again urge members of the public to come forward if they have information that could help solve the case. Wales was shot and killed the night of October 11, 2001, as he worked on a computer in the basement of his Queen Anne neighborhood home.  If Wales was killed because of his work as a federal prosecutor, it remains the only unsolved murder of a federal prosecutor because of his work. The Department of Justice and the National Association of Former U.S. Attorneys are offering a $2.5 million reward for information leading to the arrest and conviction of a subject in this case. “I still remember hearing about this murder twenty-five years ago while I was serving as an Army Judge Advocate at Fort Lewis.  This crime had a tremendous impact on the entire U.S. Attorney community and we have not forgotten.  The FBI and U.S. Attorney’s Office continue to devote resources to this active investigation,” said Acting U.S. Attorney Neil Floyd. “We are committed to using all tools available including new computer Super Intelligence to bring those responsible to justice. Now is the time to come forward if you have information that could prove useful in solving this case. The $2.5 million reward for information leading to the arrest and conviction is a real offer and should provide an incentive to do the right thing.” “For 25 years, the FBI has continued to actively pursue those responsible for the murder of AUSA Wales,” said W. Mike Herrington, Special Agent in Charge of the FBI Seattle field office. “Tom was one of us and a valued member of this community, which makes this a case that is especially important to both Seattle and law enforcement. An attack on a federal prosecutor is an attack on our entire justice system and the American way of life. If you have information about this case, now is the time to speak up. We are still receiving tips and pursuing all leads so that we can finally bring justice for Tom and his family. Don’t let one of those tips bring the FBI to you before you can report what you know on your own terms.” Acting U.S. Attorney Floyd and Special Agent in Charge Herrington went to the former Wales home today to get a briefing. Those close to the investigation explained where they believe the shooter stood when firing the shots, what was the apparent escape route, and how the site has changed over the intervening 25 years, altering the landscape. The Seattle Prosecutor Murder (SEPROM) Task Force is now a joint effort by the FBI, the Seattle Police Department, the Department of Justice, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Western District of Washington and the King County Prosecuting Attorney’s Office. The task force is also leveraging emerging and evolving technologies in the effort. Anyone with information is encouraged to contact the FBI and can do so confidentially by phone at (206) 622-0460 or by e-mail at walestips@fbi.gov . Tips can also be sent to the FBI at 1110 Third Avenue, Seattle, WA, 98101. The FBI Seeking Information poster, details about the tip lines and more can be found at https://www.fbi.gov/wanted/seeking-info/thomas-crane-wales . With more information about the case available here: https://www.fbi.gov/news/stories/wales-investigation-help-us-find-a-killer Contact Press contact for the U.S. Attorney’s Office is Communications Director Emily Langlie at (206) 553-4110 or Emily.Langlie@usdoj.gov . Updated October 9, 2026 Topic Violent Crime Component USAO - Washington, Western

title: Maryland Man Facing Federal Indictment for Role in COVID-19 Healthcare Fraud Scheme Totaling More Than $100M
body: Press Release Maryland Man Facing Federal Indictment for Role in COVID-19 Healthcare Fraud Scheme Totaling More Than $100M Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Maryland Greenbelt , Maryland – A federal grand jury indicted a Maryland man, today, in connection with a COVID-19 healthcare fraud scam. Marc Aaron Potash, 57, of Rockville, is charged with conspiracy to commit healthcare fraud and seven counts of healthcare fraud. The charges stem from Potash submitting false and fraudulent claims to Medicare, Medicaid, the Federal Employees Health Benefits Program (FEHBP), and other insurers for at-home, self-administered COVID-19 tests. Potash is also charged with five counts of conducting transactions in criminally derived proceeds. This prosecution is part of the Trump Administration’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud. Kelly O. Hayes, U.S Attorney for the District of Maryland, announced the indictment with Special Agent in Charge Darren B. Cox, FBI Washington Field Office; Inspector General T. March Bell, U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Inspector General (HHS-OIG); and Michael R. Esser, Deputy Inspector General Performing the Duties of the Inspector General, Office of Personnel Management, Office of the Inspector General (OPM-OIG). According to the indictment, between January 2022 and May 2026, Potash allegedly conspired with others to personally enrich himself and maximize the financial success of Tiero, LLC, a company located in Gaithersburg, Maryland. Through the conspiracy, Potash, Tiero’s founder and chief executive officer, and his co-conspirators schemed to obtain money through false and fraudulent representations to insurers. The indictment further alleges that as part of the healthcare fraud scheme, Potash and his co-conspirators sent false emails, letters, and paperwork to the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) to obtain a Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) certification for Tiero. As part of the conspiracy, Potash and his co-conspirators submitted documents that falsely portrayed Tiero’s medical providers performing on-site COVID-19 testing at the company’s purported lab.  The co-conspirators then used Tiero’s CLIA license to submit fraudulent claims to insurers that listed false dates of service, a fake place of service, and a phony rendering provider for COVID-19 tests that would have been administered or analyzed by a provider at Tiero. However, in reality, Potash and his co-conspirators merely shipped over-the-counter, self-administered COVID-19 tests to insured individuals across the country.  In total, Potash and his co-conspirators caused the submission of more than $100 million in false and fraudulent healthcare claims, resulting in more than $50 million in insurance payments to Tiero. The indictment also alleges that Potash engaged in multiple monetary transactions in criminally derived property.  This included Potash purchasing a Range Rover, Mercedes-Benz, and $4 million real property in Beallsville, Maryland, along with two security transfers totaling more than $4 million and $8 million, respectively. An indictment is not a finding of guilt.  Individuals charged by indictment are presumed innocent until proven guilty at a later criminal proceeding. If convicted, Potash faces a maximum of 10 years in federal prison for conspiracy to commit healthcare fraud, each count of healthcare fraud, and each count of conducting transactions in criminally derived proceeds. Actual sentences for federal crimes are typically less than the maximum penalties. A federal district court judge determines sentencing after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs. U.S. Attorney Kelly O. Hayes commended the FBI, HHS-OIG, and OPM-OIG for their work in the investigation.  Hayes also thanked Assistant U.S. Attorneys Megan S. McKoy and Joshua Rosenthal, who are prosecuting this federal case. For more information about the Maryland U.S. Attorney’s Office, its priorities, and resources available to report fraud, please visit justice.gov/usao-md and justice.gov/usao-md/report-fraud . # # # Contact Kevin Nash USAMD.Press@usdoj.gov 410-209-4946 Updated October 9, 2026 Topics COVID-Related Fraud Healthcare Fraud Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Maryland
retained_feed_body: Greenbelt , Maryland – A federal grand jury indicted a Maryland man, today, in connection with a COVID-19 healthcare fraud scam. Marc Aaron Potash, 57, of Rockville, is charged with conspiracy to commit healthcare fraud and seven counts of healthcare fraud.

title: Department of Justice Announces Federal Grants For Ulster and Clinton Counties
body: Press Release Department of Justice Announces Federal Grants For Ulster and Clinton Counties Friday, October 9, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of New York USANYN-MediaInquiry@usa.doj.gov On September 30, 2026, the counties of Ulster and Clinton received over $1 million in federal grants as part of the Byrne Discretionary Community Project Grants designed to improve the functioning of the criminal justice system announced First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III, Ulster County Sheriff Juan Figueroa, and Clinton County Sheriff David Favro. The Byrne Discretionary Grants Program provides funding for specific community projects designated for funding in the Department of Justice Appropriations Acts. Byrne Discretionary aims to improve the functioning of the criminal justice system, prevent or combat juvenile delinquency, and assist victims of crime. Clinton County will be utilizing the $500,000 granted to them to purchase a properly equipped and mission specific vessel to respond to emergencies and patrol the international border of New York and Vermont with Canada on Lake Champlain. Ulster County received $794,000 for the Sheriff’s policing equipment and technology upgrades project. The money will modernize emergency communications, investigations, corrections, crisis response and field operations across the predominantly rural county. The Sheriff’s Office can now procure and implement next-generation 911 and phone system capabilities, secure a crisis intervention and overdose data platform, mobile device forensic technology, a handheld Raman-based drug identification device, camera and automated license please reader infrastructure, and AI-supported report drafting. This will result in safer drug identification, stronger crisis follow up, better correctional awareness and more coordinated countywide public safety operations. First Assistant United States Attorney Sarcone stated, “We are proud to announce the federal grants awarded to Ulster County and Clinton County. While these counties are on the exact opposite sides of the Northern District of New York, working with state and local law enforcement is essential to keeping our entire district safe. Having Lake Champlain adequately patrolled is essential to protecting the Canadian border, which is considered the most serious threat to national security of any border today in the United States of America. Ulster County sits in the heart of the Hudson Valley with a significant portion covering Interstate-87, a known drug trafficking route. My office is proud to collaborate with Sheriff Figueroa to keep all residents of the Hudson Valley safe.” Ulster County Sheriff Juan Figueroa stated, “The Ulster County Sheriff’s Office is thankful to our partners in federal law enforcement for this funding. Teamwork is essential in achieving the Byrne Discretionary Grants goal of improving the criminal justice system. I look forward to future collaborations with the United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of New York. The historical prosecutions between the Ulster Regional Gang Enforcement Narcotics Team (U.R.G.E.N.T.) and the federal government have made Ulster County a safer place, and the new funding will ensure the safety for my community going forward.” Clinton County Sheriff David Favro stated, “Keeping the beautiful waters of Lake Champlain safe for our residents and guests is a critical mission of the Sheriff’s office. Receiving this grant for $500,000.00 will allow the Clinton County Sheriff’s Office to purchase an appropriately equipped marine vessel to respond to a variety of emergencies on Lake Champlain in addition to patrolling the international open waters that border Canada and Vermont.” Updated October 9, 2026 Component USAO - New York, Northern

title: CMORG holds sector-wide cloud outage simulation exercise
body:

Accept recommended cookies Proceed with necessary cookies only Skip to main content CMORG holds sector-wide cloud outage simulation exercise The Cross-Market Operational Resilience Group (CMORG) yesterday (8 October 2026) completed its biennial simulation exercise, known as SIMEX26, focused this year on a global cloud services disruption. Published on  
        09 October 2026 News Release The Cross-Market Operational Resilience Group (CMORG) yesterday (8 October 2026) completed its biennial simulation exercise, known as SIMEX26, focused this year on a global cloud services disruption. The group – chaired by the Bank of England (the Bank) and UK Finance, with participation from HM Treasury, the Financial Conduct Authority and the wider financial sector – met to undertake a wide-ranging crisis management exercise, with the 38 largest and most systemically important banks and market infrastructure operators involved. The exercise, which was opened by the Economic Secretary to the Treasury and hosted by the London Stock Exchange Group, involved firms working alongside the financial authorities to respond to a scenario focusing on global disruption to cloud-based services. It also included a live meeting of the Bank-chaired Cross Market Business Continuity Group, which provides strategic direction to the sector’s collective response to systemic incidents. The Bank now expects firms to take action based on the exercise to further strengthen their resilience and ability to respond to severe operational and cyber scenarios. Katharine Braddick, Deputy Governor of Prudential Regulation at the Bank of England and CEO of the Prudential Regulation Authority said: "This was an important demonstration of the UK financial sector's commitment to operational resilience. The level of collaboration reflects the priority firms place on maintaining critical services in the face of disruption. That preparedness is essential to safeguarding financial stability." David Postings, Chief Executive of UK Finance, said: “Maintaining resilience across the financial sector is critical to supporting confidence, stability, and growth in the UK economy. SIMEX 2026 enabled us to collectively strengthen preparedness and ensure the sector is better equipped to respond to significant disruptive events while continuing to deliver essential services to customers.” Economic Secretary to the Treasury Lucy Rigby said: “The operational resilience of our world-leading financial services sector is core to maintaining financial stability. “I’m grateful to all participants in SIMEX26 as we look to collectively enhance our defences against disruption, and safeguard stability and confidence.” The SIMEX programme supports the financial sector’s operational resilience by rehearsing the response to the most challenging scenarios. Previous exercises, including those in 2022 and 2024, considered cyber-attacks against a major bank, as well as critical infrastructure disruption outside the financial sector. SIMEX 26 builds on work done by the Bank of England, working in collaboration with the financial authorities and industry through CMORG, to boost operational resilience in financial services. In recent months, this has included strengthening third party engagement and resilience, enabling secure innovation in response to AI and other emerging technologies, and enhancing cyber preparedness, response and recovery for the most severe disruption scenarios. Notes to editors 1. SIMEX 26 and CMORG’s wider programme to develop financial sector capabilities supports the aims of both financial authorities and firms to ensure collective response tools are in place to respond to disruptive events. This improves the operational resilience of the financial sector and promotes a stable financial system that the public can depend on. 2. CMORG enhances the operational resilience of the UK financial sector through collective action, and is supported by specialist industry groups. It achieves this through the identification of systemic risks, the development of solutions to support sector-wide mitigation strategies and sharing capabilities and knowledge across the sector. 3. As part of this work, CMORG oversees the approach for sector-wide response to systemic incidents through the Sector Response Framework (SRF). The SRF is a key component exercised through SIMEX to ensure the UK’s financial services industry is ready to respond effectively and in a coordinated manner to severe disruption. 4. The scenario was not informed by any specific threat information but was developed alongside a range of industry experts. title: Study in The Lancet suggests AI could improve patient-physician relationships.
body: Study in The Lancet suggests AI could improve patient-physician relationships. Mike Schaekermann Research Lead Oct 08, 2026 Can AI safely assess patients’ needs before they step into a doctor’s office? A study led by researchers at Google and Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center (BIDMC) and published in The Lancet today, offers an encouraging first look. As Google’s first-ever publication in the main journal of The Lancet, this research marks a significant milestone. In a real-world clinical study at BIDMC’s ambulatory primary care clinic, 98 patients consulted AMIE , our research diagnostic AI chatbot, ahead of urgent care visits. Supervising physicians monitored the interactions in real time, and not a single conversation needed to be interrupted based on predefined safety criteria. And clinicians reported that the AI summaries helped them prepare for visits in 75% of cases and influenced their approach to care in more than half. AMIE’s differential diagnoses also matched the doctors’ final diagnoses 90% of the time. While larger clinical trials are needed to assess patient-facing AI at scale, the findings suggest the potential for AI to enhance the patient-physician relationship and ease the strain on healthcare workers. And they demonstrate meaningful progress as we push the boundaries of what’s possible for AI in science and health . Read the complete research paper in The Lancet .
retained_feed_body: A peer-reviewed study in The Lancet evaluates Google's AMIE medical AI in a real-world primary care clinic.

title: Into the Omniverse: How Developers Turn Ideas Into Simulations With Frontier AI Agents
body: Into the Omniverse: How Developers Turn Ideas Into Simulations With Frontier AI Agents See how developers are combining AI agents with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to build simulation applications, test physical behavior and guide improvements. October 8, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Your browser doesn't support HTML5 video. Here is a link to the video instead. Turning a simulation idea into a working application means assembling assets, connecting physics and rendering, and checking that the scene behaves as intended. Developers are combining frontier AI models with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to help carry out that work — building applications for exploring scenarios, investigating failures and improving designs. Developers direct AI agents through natural-language instructions, review results and guide changes. Omniverse libraries provide GPU-accelerated physics, rendering and sensor simulation capabilities. Explore the projects below to see frontier AI models such as GPT-6 Astra at work, and check back for new examples from NVIDIA teams and developers across the ecosystem. Build a Humanoid Simulator for a Warehouse Environment 🔗 https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Humanoid-Warehouse.mp4 Explore a gamified, physics-based control of a humanoid robot in first- and third-person view. Before automating warehouse tasks, developers need an interactive simulation environment to explore task behavior and evaluate how the work gets done. Frank DeLise, Omniverse product manager at NVIDIA, used Astra to turn a SimReady warehouse and humanoid robot into an interactive simulator with first- and third-person views. DeLise directed Astra to connect NVIDIA Omniverse libraries for physics ( ovphysx ), scene updates ( ovstage ), rendering ( ovrtx ) and the user interface ( ovui ). He also used Astra with SimReady ( simready-foundation ) to create the physical scene in simulation. Astra then generated animation and application code to bring those capabilities together. Learn how to prepare and validate SimReady robot assets with frontier AI models and NVIDIA Omniverse libraries. Connect an Autonomous-Driving Testing Workflow 🔗 https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/zero-to-alpamayo-under-10MB.mp4 Changing a scene, sensor or driving model can significantly affect autonomous-vehicle simulations. Doyub Kim, a manager on the simulation technology team at NVIDIA, asked Astra to build Zero to Alpamayo — a reusable simulation environment based on San Francisco’s Market Street. Kim directed Astra to map out the workflow, then connect asset creation, traffic, Omniverse RTX sensor simulation and Alpamayo driving in stages, checking each integration. The resulting prototype was a testing ground for comparing models and tracing how scene or sensor changes affect downstream driving behavior. A separate Cosmos3-Nano experiment varied weather and lighting in recorded simulation videos, allowing Kim to compare the driving model’s responses to the same scenario under different conditions. Use Sensor Differences to Create and Improve Digital Twins 🔗 https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/0_00-0_004-hubble_rivermark_Real_Sim_no_loop.mp4 Comparing recorded and simulated camera and lidar outputs gives developers key performance indicator-based feedback for refining a scene. To test robots and autonomous vehicles, developers need to know how closely simulated sensors match real ones. Ashley Reid, who works on RTX sensor validation at NVIDIA, directed Astra and Claude Fable 5 agents to compare ovrtx camera and raw LiDAR outputs with recorded data. The agents created two digital twins from scratch and improved two existing ones. Over about three days, Reid guided an iterative workflow in which agents measured differences, created or modified OpenUSD scenes, and checked the results. Changes addressed missing objects, geometry and materials, with acceptance depending on camera and LiDAR metrics. This gives developers a way to use measured discrepancies to guide scene creation and improvement. Start by rendering an OpenUSD scene with the ovrtx minimal Python example , then define a sensor measure to compare with recorded data. Robo Olympics: Test Robot Skills With Simulation 🔗 Teaching robots new movements means checking whether those actions work under physical constraints. Tae Kim, who leads NVIDIA Omniverse engineering and product, used sports videos and natural-language instructions to guide Astra in building Robo Olympics, an experimental project that tests simulated Unitree G1 humanoids performing sports movements. Under Kim’s direction, Astra built controllers and refined them through physics trials. Newton Physics Engine simulated behavior, the open source NVIDIA Warp framework accelerated calculations and ovrtx rendered scenes and virtual-camera images. In one experiment, the robot cleared a single hurdle in 64 of 100 simulation trials. The trials gave Kim feedback for improving the robot’s timing and control. Watch Kim explore building simulations with Astra and NVIDIA Omniverse libraries. Test Robotic Disassembly With Computer-Aided Design and Simulation 🔗 Before a robot can disassemble a product, developers need to know whether its tools can reach and remove the parts. Jens Jebens, a senior product manager for OpenUSD at NVIDIA, directed Astra to model a car suspension in PTC Onshape and configure it in NVIDIA Isaac Sim . With Astra, Jebens explored computer-aided design and tooling revisions for robots informed by simulation. The agent measured the available space and designed a wrench the robot could use to reach the suspension’s bolts. Jebens reported successful removal of a suspension component in simulation. This connects design and tooling decisions to disassembly results, offering a starting point for robot policy training. Explore the Onshape importer guide . Bring the International Space Station Into the Browser 🔗 Turning 3D models into an application requires connecting assets, live data and an interface. Nic Johns, an engineering director at NVIDIA, prompted Astra to assemble NASA assets into an OpenUSD International Space Station model with telemetry. Johns built the application with a single prompt, then used a follow-up prompt to shift the scene to Earth’s daytime side so the planet was visible. The workflow used Blender for asset preparation and Omniverse libraries for rendering ( ovrtx ), scene runtime (ovstage) and streaming (ovstream). The application brings 3D models and operational data into the browser, with Johns guiding its development through prompts and corrections. Try the Omniverse Real-Time Viewer skill . Turn Captured Rooms Into Testing Environments 🔗 A digitally reconstructed room needs editable objects and accurate physical behavior before developers can test interactions. Chirag Majithia, from the Isaac engineering applications team at NVIDIA, directed Astra to turn stereo camera captures into an editable OpenUSD studio. The workflow combined PyCuSFM, FoundationStereo and nvblox for reconstruction, with user review guiding object selection and placement. Astra assembled generated and Blender-authored assets and used USD Content Agents to configure how objects move and interact in simulation. Isaac Sim tests guided collision and contact revisions for doors and drawers. The studio connects captured geometry to interaction testing, making gaps and object behavior easier to inspect. Explore USD Content Agents. Have a simulation idea? Explore NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to start building with an AI agent. Categories: Robotics Tags: Agentic AI Into the Omniverse NVIDIA Isaac Sim Omniverse OpenUSD Physical AI Simulation Related News AI NVIDIA, Microsoft Kick Off a New Beginning for Windows PCs With RTX Spark and AI Agents Oct 7, 2026 AI Why Telecom Operators Are Building Their AI Strategy on Open Models Oct 6, 2026 AI NVIDIA DGX Spark 64GB Gives Developers More Ways to Build and Scale Local AI Oct 2, 2026 AI Infrastructure How NVIDIA GPUs Help Accelerate OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra Ultrafast Oct 1, 2026

Main Menu Toggle Button Sections Search Toggle Button Search Search Submit Button Submit Home News & Events Press Releases Press Release October 08, 2026 Federal Reserve Board announces enforcement action against American Express Company to address, among other things, the firm’s failure to sufficiently detect and report certain suspicious activity related to money laundering For release at 4:30 p.m. EDT Share The Federal Reserve Board on Thursday announced an enforcement action against American Express Company to address, among other things, the firm's failure to sufficiently detect and report certain suspicious activity related to money laundering. The Board also identified significant deficiencies in how American Express Company's enterprise-wide anti-money laundering program was implemented, in particular at the firm's subsidiary national bank. The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, the primary federal regulator of the firm's national bank, has issued a separate enforcement action against the bank. The Board's action will help ensure that the firm operates in compliance with all U.S. laws and regulations. For media inquiries, please email [email protected] or call (202) 452-2955.
